content.text:
Read, in order: Linear COR-1254 (ALL comments — especially the canary verdict
with the two structural blockers), the program status comment on COR-1252,
ENT-1601's "A1 library work MERGED" comment, and COR-1009. Mission: migrate
mirror-pipeline's legacy consume loops onto go-nuts jsconsumer (main, 832d765+)
— ONE TRAIL/PR PER CONSUMER, each independently reviewable, mergeable, and
revertable. Hard rule from the program: NO NACK Consumer CRs in this work —
that half of Track D is parked.

PHASE 0 — analysis only, no code. Inventory the four loops (worker/consumer,
webhook-forwarder, meta-fanout + lifecycle, fanoutengine). For each, document:
stream + retention type + durable name; current retry/give-up semantics
(client NakWithDelay ladders, Term sites, KV fail-index + rekick, and
ESPECIALLY any reliance on server-side InactiveThreshold reaping — the
2026-06-01 interest-stream safety valve the canary found; migrations must
preserve or consciously replace it, never silently drop it); whether a paired
DLQ + publish grant exists; and the proposed target shape. Key judgment call,
stated per loop: the jsconsumer SCAFFOLD (fetch/ack/heartbeat/shutdown
discipline) migrates always — but the GIVE-UP model does not automatically
become Retry/capture-then-Ack. A workqueue loop with a designed KV fail-index
+ rekick path keeps that give-up, migrated onto the scaffold; Retry is for
loops where dead-letter-to-DLQ is the right semantic and a DLQ pairing exists.
Where a DLQ or grant is missing, flag it as a fleet change — never widen a
grant in-place. End phase 0 with: the per-loop table, a lowest-risk-first
migration order with rationale, and whether a PR-0 (shared scaffold plumbing)
is needed so later PRs stay independent. STOP for my approval before writing
code.

PER-LOOP RULES for the migration PRs (hard-won this week, all recorded on
ENT-1601/COR-1254):
- Same durable names — no recreation, no redelivery storms.
- If the loop moves to a server-owned ladder: the failure disposition is DO
  NOTHING (measured: plain Nak redelivers in 0s; BackOff paces ack timeouts);
  ackWait = backoff[0]; the three MaxDeliver numbers must agree (consumer,
  len(backoff) with tail-repeat semantics, Retry) — validate with go-nuts'
  exported jsconsumer.Schedule, never hand arithmetic.
- Each trail body carries a before/after timing-contract table (the old
  effective ladder vs the new one) and the InactiveThreshold decision for
  that loop, explicitly.
- No bare Term anywhere. Settle-outcome observability (metrics/logs) per the
  entire-search adoption pattern (trail #131 is the reference).
- Real-broker tests where give-up semantics change (the embedded nats-server
  pattern from go-nuts internal/brokersemantics).
- Full gate per repo conventions; one trail per loop; branches for later
  loops base on main (or on PR-0 once merged), never stacked on each other.
- Merge cadence is mine: after each merge I'll watch staging before green-
  lighting the next.
I'll start by reading the Linear issues in the order you specified.

22	)

24	const (
25		consumerFailureDelay = 30 * time.Second
26		consumerMaxDeliver   = 10
27		consumerAckWait      = 15 * time.Minute
28		consumerBackoffInit  = 1 * time.Second
29		consumerBackoffMax   = 30 * time.Second
30		// consumerInProgressInterval paces in-progress ack extensions while a
31		// long sync is running. Derived from consumerAckWait so any change to
32		// the ack budget automatically widens the extension cadence; /3 gives
33		// two extension attempts within one ack window before redelivery.
34		consumerInProgressInterval = consumerAckWait / 3
35		// defaultSyncTimeout bounds one sync attempt end-to-end (override via
36		// ENTIRE_WORKER_SYNC_TIMEOUT; "0" disables). The git smart-HTTP client
37		// has no timeout of its own, and the InProgress extender refreshes the
38		// ack deadline for as long as sync runs — so without this budget a
39		// black-holed connection (established, then silently dropped) wedges
40		// the replica forever AND suppresses redelivery: the serial consume
41		// loop never fetches again and the extender keeps the message owned.
42		// Generous on purpose: a legitimate multi-GB initial clone must fit.
43		defaultSyncTimeout = 30 * time.Minute
44	)
45	
46	type repoSyncer interface {
47		sync(ctx context.Context, req syncRequest) error
48	}
49	
50	// ackableMsg is the subset of *nats.Msg the disposition logic uses to ack a
51	// message. A seam so the Term/Nak/Ack decisions are unit-testable without a
52	// live JetStream subscription (*nats.Msg satisfies it implicitly).
53	type ackableMsg interface {
54		Ack(opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
55		Term(opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
56		NakWithDelay(delay time.Duration, opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
57		Metadata() (*nats.MsgMetadata, error)
58	}
59	
60	// failureIndex is the failure-index surface the consumer depends on. An
61	// interface so a test can inject a fake whose RecordFailure errors, locking the
62	// fail-open invariant — a KV write failure must Term (not Nak) and surface via
63	// record_failed{cause} (*failindex.Index satisfies it).
64	type failureIndex interface {
65		RecordFailure(ulid string, fs failindex.FailedSync, seq uint64, now time.Time) (recorded bool, err error)
66		ClearOnSuccess(ulid string, successSeq uint64) (bool, error)
67	}
68	
69	// completionPublisher publishes a terminal mirror-completion (the mirror_done
70	// op on the in-cell repo_ops_v1 stream) so the co-located regional entire-core
71	// can flip mirror_repos.status (processing → ready|failed). An interface so the
72	// disposition logic stays unit-testable without a live JetStream, and so a
73	// nil publisher degrades to the pre-completion behaviour (*donejobs.Publisher
74	// satisfies it).
75	type completionPublisher interface {
76		PublishCompletion(ctx context.Context, jurisdiction, cluster string, job donejobs.Job) error
77	}
78	
79	type subscriptionConfig struct {
80		subject string
81		durable string
82	}
83	
84	type consumer struct {
85		js                  nats.JetStreamContext
86		clusterID           string
87		jurisdiction        string
88		sourceClusterDomain string
89		syncer              repoSyncer
90		metrics             *workerMetrics
91		// health drives the severity of subscribe/fetch failure logs: recoverable
92		// interruptions log at warn until the loop goes too long without progress.
93		health natslog.Health
94		// failidx is the mirror-sync failure index (KV). nil when the bucket could
95		// not be bound at startup — the record/clear helpers then degrade to the
96		// pre-index behaviour (bare Term / no clear) so the worker still syncs.
97		failidx failureIndex
98		// donePub publishes terminal mirror-completion events (repo_ops_v1 mirror_done op).
99		// nil when no publisher is wired (degrades to the pre-completion
100		// behaviour: ack/term as before, entire-core never learns the outcome).
101		donePub completionPublisher
102		// syncTimeout bounds one sync attempt (see defaultSyncTimeout). <= 0
103		// disables the budget.
104		syncTimeout time.Duration
105	}
106	
107	// mirrorConsumerDurable is the JetStream durable name the worker subscribes
108	// to. KEDA's nats-jetstream scaler targets the same name (the `consumer:`
109	// field in the mirror-worker ScaledObjects in fleet) so the autoscaling
110	// signal reflects exactly this worker's backlog.
111	func mirrorConsumerDurable(jurisdiction, clusterID string) string {
112		return fmt.Sprintf("mirror-git-v1-%s-%s", jurisdiction, clusterID)
113	}
114	
115	func (c *consumer) run(ctx context.Context) {
116		c.runSubscription(ctx, subscriptionConfig{
117			subject: fmt.Sprintf("%s%s.%s.>", gitjobs.SubjectPrefix, c.jurisdiction, c.clusterID),
118			durable: mirrorConsumerDurable(c.jurisdiction, c.clusterID),
119		})
120	}
121	
122	func (c *consumer) runSubscription(ctx context.Context, cfg subscriptionConfig) {
123		backoff := consumerBackoffInit
124	
125		for {
126			sub, err := c.js.PullSubscribe(cfg.subject, cfg.durable, nats.ManualAck(),
127				nats.AckWait(consumerAckWait),
128				nats.MaxDeliver(consumerMaxDeliver),
129			)
130			if err != nil {
131				c.health.SubscribeErr(ctx, "Failed to subscribe", err,
132					slog.String("subject", cfg.subject),
133					slog.String("durable", cfg.durable),
134				)
135				select {
136				case <-ctx.Done():
137					return
138				case <-time.After(backoff):
139					backoff = min(backoff*2, consumerBackoffMax)
140					continue
141				}
142			}
143			backoff = consumerBackoffInit
144			slog.Info("Consumer subscribed", slog.String("durable", cfg.durable), slog.String("subject", cfg.subject))
145	
146			c.consumeLoop(ctx, sub)
147	
148			if ctx.Err() != nil {
149				return
150			}
151		}
152	}
153	
154	func (c *consumer) consumeLoop(ctx context.Context, sub *nats.Subscription) {
155		for {
156			if ctx.Err() != nil {
157				return
158			}
159			msgs, err := sub.Fetch(1, nats.MaxWait(5*time.Second))
160			if err != nil {
161				if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) {
162					// An idle poll is progress: connected, stream merely quiet.
163					c.health.Recovered()
164					continue
165				}
166				if nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) {
167					// Connection drained/closed during shutdown — a clean exit,
168					// not a fault (COR-923).
169					return
170				}
171				c.health.Err(ctx, "Fetch error", err)
172				return
173			}
174			c.health.Recovered()
175	
176			for _, msg := range msgs {
177				c.handleMessage(ctx, msg)
178			}
179		}
180	}
181	
182	func (c *consumer) handleMessage(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
183		// Parent the consume span to the producer's trace when the publisher
184		// injected a W3C traceparent header (pkg/natsmsg.Inject). When headers
185		// are absent (older publishers, or the test /publish endpoint), Extract
186		// is a no-op and the span starts a new trace.
187		ctx = natsmsg.Extract(ctx, msg)
188	
189		ctx, span := Tracer().Start(ctx, "mirror.consume",
190			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindConsumer),
191			trace.WithAttributes(
192				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
193				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "receive"),
194				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", msg.Subject),
195			),
196		)
197		defer span.End()
198	
199		// A panic anywhere below (a nil deref in payload handling, a bug deep in
200		// the git-sync stack on a pathological repo) must NOT unwind into the
201		// consume goroutine: that crashes the process, and because the message was
202		// never acked JetStream redelivers it — so every replica that picks it up
203		// crashes in turn, turning one poison-pill job into a cluster-wide
204		// crash-loop. Recover and dispose it as a transient failure instead.
205		// Registered after span.End() so it runs first (LIFO) and can stamp the
206		// span before it closes.
207		defer func() {
208			if r := recover(); r != nil {
209				c.handlePanic(ctx, span, msg, r)
210			}
211		}()
212	
213		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
214			span.SetAttributes(
215				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(meta.Sequence.Stream)),
216				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.delivery_count", int64(meta.NumDelivered)),
217			)
218		} else {
219			slog.DebugContext(ctx, "msg.Metadata failed; span missing nats sequence attrs", slog.Any("error", err))
220		}
221	
222		// Subject is the canonical routing key — placement, source kind, and op
223		// live there, not in the body. A malformed subject means the broker
224		// routed something we shouldn't have received; terminate without retry.
225		parsed, err := gitjobs.ParseSubject(msg.Subject)
226		if err != nil {
227			span.RecordError(err)
228			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "parse subject")
229			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
230			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Bad subject, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
231			_ = msg.Term()
232			return
233		}
234		span.SetAttributes(parsed.SpanAttrs()...)
235	
236		j, err := gitjobs.UnmarshalFor(parsed.SourceKind, msg.Data)
237		if err != nil {
238			span.RecordError(err)
239			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "unmarshal job")
240			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
241			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Bad job payload, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
242			// Terminate WITH the failure-index record + failed-completion publish,
243			// not a bare Term: UnmarshalFor returns the decoded body alongside a
244			// validation error, so a kind/body mismatch (e.g. a github-shaped body
245			// on an entiredb subject) still carries the target ULID that keys the
246			// record — the same terminal handling the pre-kind-aware code gave
247			// these messages at the source-kind gate. recordTerminal and
248			// publishFailed no-op safely on an empty ULID (pure JSON garbage).
249			c.terminate(ctx, msg, j.Target.ULID, msg.Subject, msg.Data, failindex.ReasonValidation, failindex.SourceWorkerValidation, err)
250			return
251		}
252		c.handleGitJob(ctx, span, msg, parsed, j)
253	}

255	// handlePanic disposes of a message whose handler panicked. It Naks (rather
256	// than Terms) so redelivery is bounded by consumerMaxDeliver and the existing
257	// MAX_DELIVERIES path + advisory backstop still record the eventual terminal
258	// failure into the index for re-kick: a transient cause recovers on a later
259	// delivery, and a deterministic one dead-ends — both WITHOUT crashing the
260	// process. The stack is logged once here (the recover site) so the poison-pill
261	// payload is diagnosable; the span carries entire.handler.panicked for queries.
262	func (c *consumer) handlePanic(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, m ackableMsg, recovered any) {
263		err := fmt.Errorf("panic recovered in mirror handler: %v", recovered)
264		span.RecordError(err)
265		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "handler panic")
266		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.handler.panicked", true))
267		slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Recovered panic in mirror handler; naking message (bounded by MaxDeliver)",
268			slog.Any("panic", recovered),
269			slog.String("stack", string(debug.Stack())),
270		)
271		c.metrics.recordPanic(ctx)
272		_ = m.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
273	}

275	func (c *consumer) handleGitJob(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg *nats.Msg, parsed gitjobs.ParsedSubject, j gitjobs.Job) {
276		span.SetAttributes(j.SpanAttrs()...)
277		logAttrs := append(parsed.LogAttrs(), j.LogAttrs()...)
278		slog.LogAttrs(ctx, slog.LevelInfo, "Processing git job", logAttrs...)
279	
280		if parsed.Op != gitjobs.OpSyncRepo {
281			err := permanentErr(fmt.Errorf("unsupported operation %q", parsed.Op))
282			span.RecordError(err)
283			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "unsupported operation")
284			span.SetAttributes(
285				attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", true),
286				attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true),
287			)
288			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Unsupported operation, terminating", slog.String("operation", string(parsed.Op)))
289			c.terminate(ctx, msg, j.Target.ULID, msg.Subject, msg.Data, failindex.ReasonValidation, failindex.SourceWorkerValidation, err)
290			return
291		}
292	
293		var sreq syncRequest
294		switch parsed.SourceKind {
295		case gitjobs.SourceKindGithub:
296			installationID, err := gitjobs.ParseGithubInstallationAuthRef(j.Source.AuthRef)
297			if err != nil {
298				err := permanentErr(err)
299				span.RecordError(err)
300				span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "invalid git source auth ref")
301				span.SetAttributes(
302					attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", true),
303					attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true),
304				)
305				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Invalid git source auth ref, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
306				c.terminate(ctx, msg, j.Target.ULID, msg.Subject, msg.Data, failindex.ReasonValidation, failindex.SourceWorkerValidation, err)
307				return
308			}
309			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int64("entire.installation_id", installationID))
310			sreq = syncRequest{
311				SourceKind:     gitjobs.SourceKindGithub,
312				SourceOwner:    j.Source.Owner,
313				SourceRepo:     j.Source.Repo,
314				InstallationID: installationID,
315				TargetULID:     j.Target.ULID,
316			}
317		case gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB:
318			// Decode validation bounds the URL shape; admission here bounds where
319			// the worker may present its client certificate. The environment-wide
320			// domain is derived from Fleet's trusted local target configuration,
321			// so sibling clusters are accepted without a per-cluster allowlist.
322			sourceClusterParent, err := admitEntireDBSourceURL(j.Source.URL, c.sourceClusterDomain)
323			if err != nil {
324				err = permanentErr(fmt.Errorf("admit entiredb source: %w", err))
325				span.RecordError(err)
326				span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "entiredb source outside allowed domain")
327				span.SetAttributes(
328					attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", true),
329					attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true),
330				)
331				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Entiredb source rejected, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
332				c.terminate(ctx, msg, j.Target.ULID, msg.Subject, msg.Data, failindex.ReasonValidation, failindex.SourceWorkerValidation, err)
333				return
334			}
335			span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.source_cluster_parent", sourceClusterParent))
336			sreq = syncRequest{
337				SourceKind:          gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB,
338				SourceURL:           j.Source.URL,
339				SourceClusterParent: sourceClusterParent,
340				TargetULID:          j.Target.ULID,
341			}
342		default:
343			// UnmarshalFor already rejects unknown kinds, so this is defensive.
344			err := permanentErr(fmt.Errorf("unsupported git source kind %q", parsed.SourceKind))
345			span.RecordError(err)
346			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "unsupported git source")
347			span.SetAttributes(
348				attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", true),
349				attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true),
350			)
351			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Unsupported git source, terminating", slog.String("source_kind", string(parsed.SourceKind)))
352			c.terminate(ctx, msg, j.Target.ULID, msg.Subject, msg.Data, failindex.ReasonValidation, failindex.SourceWorkerValidation, err)
353			return
354		}
355	
356		// A single sync on a multi-GB repo regularly exceeds consumerAckWait, so
357		// extend the ack deadline on a sub-AckWait cadence while sync runs. The
358		// extender's lifetime is exactly the sync call: explicit stop right after
359		// sync returns keeps it from overlapping with Ack/Term/Nak in
360		// disposeResult (an InProgress racing an Ack would log a spurious warn),
361		// and a deferred stop covers the panic path. stopExtender is idempotent,
362		// so the two paths don't fight. We deliberately don't raise AckWait: if a
363		// pod dies mid-job we still want redelivery within the configured window.
364		stopExtender := startInProgressExtender(ctx, msg, consumerInProgressInterval)
365		defer stopExtender()
366	
367		// Bound the attempt. git-sync is context-aware end to end (every HTTP
368		// request is built with NewRequestWithContext), so the deadline aborts
369		// in-flight transfers — which also stops the extender above, restoring
370		// AckWait expiry as the backstop. A timeout classifies as transient →
371		// Nak; a repo that exceeds the budget on every attempt exhausts
372		// MaxDeliver and lands in the failure index (reason=max_deliveries).
373		syncCtx := ctx
374		if c.syncTimeout > 0 {
375			var cancel context.CancelFunc
376			syncCtx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, c.syncTimeout)
377			defer cancel()
378		}
379		// Saturation + tail-latency instrumentation. syncStarted increments the
380		// in-flight gauge and its deferred done() decrements it on every exit
381		// (including a panic recovered upstream), keeping mirror.sync.active
382		// balanced. elapsed is the wall-time around exactly the sync call; it is
383		// threaded into disposeResult so mirror.sync.duration_seconds is tagged with
384		// the real disposition (a slow ack vs a slow nak). Measured here, recorded
385		// there, so the latency sample and the outcome label share one source.
386		doneActive := c.metrics.syncStarted(ctx, c.jurisdiction)
387		defer doneActive() // deferred so the decrement runs on every exit, including a sync panic recovered in handleMessage; otherwise the in-flight gauge leaks and biases utilization toward saturation
388		start := time.Now()
389		err := c.syncer.sync(syncCtx, sreq)
390		elapsed := time.Since(start)
391		stopExtender()
392		if err != nil && errors.Is(syncCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) && ctx.Err() == nil {
393			// Our budget fired (not a process shutdown: the parent is still
394			// alive). Wrap explicitly transient so the disposition can't be
395			// swayed by however the aborted transfer's error happens to read,
396			// and stamp the span so timed-out syncs are queryable.
397			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.deadline_exceeded", true))
398			err = transientErr(fmt.Errorf("sync exceeded the %v budget: %w", c.syncTimeout, err))
399		}
400	
401		// Tag concurrent-ref races so they stay queryable in traces even though
402		// (below) they're deliberately not marked as span errors.
403		if isConcurrentRefError(err) {
404			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.raced", true))
405		}
406		// Mark the span as an error only for genuine failures. Benign cases —
407		// errSourceNoRefs (empty source, acked as a no-op) and a redelivering
408		// concurrent-ref race — are excluded so they don't inflate the
409		// mirror.consume APM error rate, matching their exclusion from the outcome
410		// metric. See shouldMarkSpanError.
411		if shouldMarkSpanError(err, isLastDelivery(msg)) {
412			span.RecordError(err)
413			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "sync failed")
414			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", isPermanentError(err)))
415		}
416		// A re-kicked job (cmd/rekicker) carries the Mirror-Rekick header; on success
417		// the clear is tagged cleared{via=rekick} vs via=normal. Header.Get only
418		// exists on *nats.Msg, not the ackableMsg disposition seam, so read it here
419		// and thread the flag down rather than widen the interface.
420		viaRekick := msg.Header.Get(failindex.RekickHeader) != ""
421		c.disposeResult(ctx, msg, err, string(parsed.SourceKind), j.Target.ULID, msg.Subject, msg.Data, viaRekick, elapsed)
422	}
423	
424	// disposeResult applies the JetStream action for a sync result and records the
425	// outcome metrics. elapsed is the wall-time of the sync attempt (measured in
426	// handleGitJob); it is recorded on mirror.sync.duration_seconds tagged with the
427	// disposition resolved here, so the latency sample carries the real outcome.
428	func (c *consumer) disposeResult(ctx context.Context, m ackableMsg, err error, provider, ulid, subject string, payload []byte, viaRekick bool, elapsed time.Duration) {
429		seq := streamSeq(m)
430		switch classifyDisposition(err) {
431		case dispositionAck:
432			// Publish the ready completion BEFORE acking. entire-core flips
433			// mirror_repos.status (processing → ready) off this event, and once we
434			// ack the job leaves the work-queue stream and is never redelivered — so
435			// a publish lost after the ack would strand the row in 'processing'
436			// forever, hanging the CLI's status poll. publishReadyOrRetry holds the
437			// ack until the publish lands (or gives up on the final delivery); see
438			// its doc for the at-least-once rationale.
439			if !c.publishReadyOrRetry(ctx, m, provider, ulid, elapsed) {
440				return
441			}
442			c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeAck, elapsed)
443			_ = m.Ack()
444			c.clearIndex(ctx, ulid, seq, viaRekick) // repo healed → drop any stale index entry
445		case dispositionNoop:
446			// Empty source: nothing to mirror, but the mirror IS clonable (an empty
447			// repo is a valid clone target), so it's 'ready' to entire-core. Same
448			// publish-before-ack discipline as the success path. Do NOT clear the
449			// failure index here: a noop applied no refs and reconciled nothing (it
450			// is deliberately not a ref-applying success — see last_success_unix), so
451			// it must not prune a recorded terminal failure that may have left the
452			// mirror inconsistent. Only a real sync (Ack) or a re-kick that ends in
453			// one clears. A genuinely-emptied source self-heals on its next real
454			// sync, or the entry ages out via the bucket ttl.
455			if !c.publishReadyOrRetry(ctx, m, provider, ulid, elapsed) {
456				return
457			}
458			c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeNoop, elapsed)
459			_ = m.Ack()
460		case dispositionTerm:
461			// Best-effort record, then Term regardless — fail open. recordTerminal
462			// logs + counts record_failed{cause} on a KV write failure; we Term
463			// either way rather than Nak, because the failure is permanent (re-running
464			// the sync would be wasted work) and a KV outage must not wedge the
465			// consumer. Recovery of a dropped record is owned by the record_failed
466			// alert + L2 reconcile, not by holding the message.
467			c.recordTerminal(ctx, ulid, subject, payload, seq, failindex.ReasonPermanent, failindex.SourceWorkerPermanent, err)
468			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Permanent sync error, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
469			c.publishFailed(ctx, ulid) // best-effort: tell entire-core the clone won't land
470			c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeTerm, elapsed)
471			_ = m.Term()
472		case dispositionNak:
473			if isLastDelivery(m) {
474				// Final delivery: JetStream won't redeliver past consumerMaxDeliver,
475				// so this is terminal. Best-effort record (max_deliveries), then Term —
476				// fail open (recordTerminal surfaces a write failure via record_failed).
477				c.recordTerminal(ctx, ulid, subject, payload, seq, failindex.ReasonMaxDeliveries, failindex.SourceWorkerExhausted, err)
478				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Sync failed; deliveries exhausted, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
479				c.publishFailed(ctx, ulid) // best-effort: clone exhausted retries, won't land
480				c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeTerm, elapsed)
481				_ = m.Term()
482				return
483			}
484			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Sync failed", slog.Any("error", err))
485			c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeNak, elapsed)
486			_ = m.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
487		case dispositionRaced:
488			// Target ref moved between this job's plan and its push — a second sync
489			// of the same repo won the race (rapid webhooks, or a webhook
490			// overlapping the rekicker). Redeliver like a nak so the next delivery
491			// re-plans against the new tip and applies cleanly (usually a no-op,
492			// since the winner already mirrored the same source state), but record
493			// outcomeRaced + WARN so it stays out of the sync-failure alert's
494			// nak+term numerator: it self-heals and pages no one.
495			//
496			// Final-delivery escalation is identical to the nak path for the failure
497			// index + alert: if a repo somehow races every delivery to exhaustion the
498			// contention is no longer benign, so we record terminal (max_deliveries)
499			// and label outcome=term — that DOES reach the alert. Fail open on the
500			// index write exactly like dispositionNak.
501			//
502			// But we deliberately do NOT publish a 'failed' completion here. A raced
503			// error (ErrTargetRefMoved) means the target ref moved under us — i.e. a
504			// CONCURRENT sync of the same ULID is racing us, and one of those is the
505			// likely winner that publishes 'ready'. Emitting 'failed' would describe
506			// contention as an unclonable mirror; entire-core's MarkReady would heal
507			// it on the winner's event anyway, but skipping 'failed' avoids the
508			// misleading transient flip entirely. If no sibling ever wins (pathological
509			// — they can't all lose), status lingers at 'processing' and the failure
510			// index/alert still fire.
511			if isLastDelivery(m) {
512				c.recordTerminal(ctx, ulid, subject, payload, seq, failindex.ReasonMaxDeliveries, failindex.SourceWorkerExhausted, err)
513				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Sync kept racing on target ref; deliveries exhausted, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
514				c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeTerm, elapsed)
515				_ = m.Term()
516				return
517			}
518			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Sync raced on target ref; will retry", slog.Any("error", err))
519			c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeRaced, elapsed)
520			_ = m.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
521		}
522	}
523	
524	// publishReadyOrRetry publishes the StatusReady completion and reports whether
525	// the caller may proceed to Ack. It returns true when the publish lands (or
526	// when no publisher is wired, or there's no ULID to key on) — the ack is safe.
527	//
528	// On a publish failure it does NOT ack: the completion is the only signal
529	// entire-core gets that the clone finished, and acking would drop it for good.
530	// Instead it Naks (except on the final delivery), so JetStream redelivers, the
531	// next attempt re-runs the idempotent sync (a near-noop — refs already
532	// applied), and re-publishes. entire-core's status write is itself idempotent,
533	// so a duplicate ready is harmless. On the FINAL delivery it gives up and acks
534	// anyway (returns true): the sync genuinely succeeded, so terming + recording a
535	// max_deliveries "sync failure" would be a lie, and a Nak past MaxDeliver just
536	// dead-letters the job. The row stays 'processing' until a later sync (or a
537	// reconcile backstop) re-publishes — surfaced via mirror.done.published{result=error}.
538	func (c *consumer) publishReadyOrRetry(ctx context.Context, m ackableMsg, provider, ulid string, elapsed time.Duration) (proceed bool) {
539		if c.donePub == nil || ulid == "" {
540			return true
541		}
542		err := c.donePub.PublishCompletion(ctx, c.jurisdiction, c.clusterID, donejobs.Job{
543			RepoULID: ulid,
544			Status:   donejobs.StatusReady,
545		})
546		if err == nil {
547			c.metrics.recordDonePublished(ctx, string(donejobs.StatusReady), true)
548			return true
549		}
550		c.metrics.recordDonePublished(ctx, string(donejobs.StatusReady), false)
551		if isLastDelivery(m) {
552			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Failed to publish mirror completion on final delivery; acking anyway (sync succeeded, status left processing)",
553				slog.String("target_ulid", ulid), slog.Any("error", err))
554			return true
555		}
556		slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Failed to publish mirror completion; naking to retry", slog.String("target_ulid", ulid), slog.Any("error", err))
557		c.metrics.recordSyncOutcome(ctx, provider, c.jurisdiction, outcomeNak, elapsed)
558		_ = m.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
559		return false
560	}
561	
562	// publishFailed publishes the StatusFailed completion on a best-effort basis:
563	// any error is logged and counted, never escalated. The message is already
564	// being Term'd (a permanent or retry-exhausted failure), so re-running the
565	// doomed sync to retry the publish would be wasted work; a lost 'failed' just
566	// leaves entire-core's row in 'processing' until the CLI's poll times out
567	// client-side — degraded, not incorrect. Mirrors the fail-open discipline
568	// recordTerminal already uses for the KV index.
569	func (c *consumer) publishFailed(ctx context.Context, ulid string) {
570		if c.donePub == nil || ulid == "" {
571			return
572		}
573		err := c.donePub.PublishCompletion(ctx, c.jurisdiction, c.clusterID, donejobs.Job{
574			RepoULID: ulid,
575			Status:   donejobs.StatusFailed,
576		})
577		if err != nil {
578			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Failed to publish mirror failed-completion (best-effort, terminating anyway)",
579				slog.String("target_ulid", ulid), slog.Any("error", err))
580			c.metrics.recordDonePublished(ctx, string(donejobs.StatusFailed), false)
581			return
582		}
583		c.metrics.recordDonePublished(ctx, string(donejobs.StatusFailed), true)
584	}
585	
586	// disposition is the JetStream action disposeResult takes for a sync result.
587	type disposition int
588	
589	const (
590		dispositionAck   disposition = iota // success → Ack
591		dispositionNoop                     // benign empty-source no-op → Ack
592		dispositionTerm                     // permanent failure → Term (no redelivery)
593		dispositionNak                      // transient failure → Nak (redeliver)
594		dispositionRaced                    // benign concurrent-ref miss → Nak (redeliver), but counted as outcomeRaced not outcomeNak
595	)
596	
597	// classifyDisposition maps a sync() result to its JetStream disposition. Pure
598	// (no IO) so the ack/noop/term/nak decision is unit-testable independent of a
599	// live subscription; disposeResult owns the side effects.
600	func classifyDisposition(err error) disposition {
601		switch {
602		case err == nil:
603			return dispositionAck
604		case errors.Is(err, errSourceNoRefs):
605			return dispositionNoop
606		case isPermanentError(err):
607			return dispositionTerm
608		case isConcurrentRefError(err):
609			// Checked after isPermanentError so a 4xx that happens to echo a
610			// concurrent-ref phrase still terminates; concurrent-ref errors are
611			// never marked permanent, so this only ever reclassifies the transient
612			// (would-be-nak) tail.
613			return dispositionRaced
614		default:
615			return dispositionNak
616		}
617	}
618	
619	func isPermanentError(err error) bool {
620		var se *syncError
621		if errors.As(err, &se) {
622			return se.permanent
623		}
624		return false
625	}
626	
627	// streamSeq returns the message's JetStream stream sequence, or 0 if metadata
628	// is unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test message). Used as the failure-index
629	// dedup token and the clear-on-success ordering guard.
630	func streamSeq(msg ackableMsg) uint64 {
631		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
632			return meta.Sequence.Stream
633		}
634		return 0
635	}
636	
637	// isLastDelivery reports whether this is the final delivery before JetStream
638	// stops redelivering (NumDelivered has reached consumerMaxDeliver).
639	func isLastDelivery(msg ackableMsg) bool {
640		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
641			return meta.NumDelivered >= consumerMaxDeliver
642		}
643		return false
644	}
645	
646	// recordTerminal makes a BEST-EFFORT write of a terminal failure to the KV
647	// index. It never gates the caller's disposal: on a KV write failure it fails
648	// open — logs and increments record_failed{cause}, and the caller Terms the
649	// message anyway rather than Nak-ing. A KV outage must not wedge the consumer or
650	// burn re-sync retries (the record-failure paths are permanent/validation/
651	// exhausted, where a re-sync is wasted or moot). Recovery of a dropped record is
652	// owned by the record_failed alert and the L2 reconcile, not by holding the
653	// message.
654	func (c *consumer) recordTerminal(ctx context.Context, ulid, subject string, payload []byte, seq uint64, reason failindex.FailureReason, source string, cause error) {
655		if c.failidx == nil {
656			// Index unbound — cannot capture this terminal failure. Surface it
657			// (depth/recorded stay flat otherwise); the caller Terms regardless.
658			c.metrics.recordIndexUnavailable(ctx, failedIndexCauseUnbound)
659			return
660		}
661		if ulid == "" {
662			// Reachable: a payload that fails json decoding entirely carries no
663			// target ULID to key a record on. Nothing to capture.
664			return
665		}
666		fs := failindex.FailedSync{
667			Subject:   subject,
668			Payload:   payload,
669			Reason:    reason,
670			Source:    source,
671			LastError: truncateError(cause),
672		}
673		recorded, err := c.failidx.RecordFailure(ulid, fs, seq, time.Now())
674		if err != nil {
675			// Fail open: log + metric, but the caller still Terms (see doc comment).
676			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Failed to record terminal failure to index; terminating anyway (fail open)",
677				slog.String("target_ulid", ulid), slog.String("reason", string(reason)), slog.Any("error", err))
678			c.metrics.recordIndexUnavailable(ctx, failedIndexCauseWriteError)
679			return
680		}
681		// Only count a genuine record — a dedup/reorder no-op (recorded=false) means
682		// the failure was already captured, so counting it would inflate recorded
683		// on a redelivery or the in-process/advisory pair.
684		if recorded {
685			c.metrics.recordIndexed(ctx, string(reason))
686		}
687	}

689	// terminate records a terminal failure (best-effort) then Terms. Used by the
690	// pre-sync validation rejects, which carry no sync-outcome metric. These are
691	// permanent failures of a well-formed job (unsupported op/source kind, bad
692	// auth ref) — the clone will never land — so publish 'failed' best-effort so
693	// entire-core flips mirror_repos.status off 'processing' rather than the CLI
694	// poll hanging until timeout.
695	func (c *consumer) terminate(ctx context.Context, m ackableMsg, ulid, subject string, payload []byte, reason failindex.FailureReason, source string, cause error) {
696		c.recordTerminal(ctx, ulid, subject, payload, streamSeq(m), reason, source, cause)
697		c.publishFailed(ctx, ulid)
698		_ = m.Term()
699	}
700	
701	// clearIndex removes the repo's failure-index entry after a successful sync.
702	// Best-effort: a failure here is logged but never fails the sync (it already
703	// succeeded; a stale entry self-heals on the next success or re-kick). viaRekick
704	// tags the cleared metric so an operator can tell re-kicker-driven recoveries
705	// (cleared{via=rekick}) from organic ones (via=normal) — the "are re-kicks
706	// healing repos?" signal.
707	func (c *consumer) clearIndex(ctx context.Context, ulid string, seq uint64, viaRekick bool) {
708		if c.failidx == nil || ulid == "" {
709			return
710		}
711		cleared, err := c.failidx.ClearOnSuccess(ulid, seq)
712		if err != nil {
713			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Failed to clear failure index after success",
714				slog.String("target_ulid", ulid), slog.Any("error", err))
715			return
716		}
717		if cleared {
718			via := clearedViaNormal
719			if viaRekick {
720				via = clearedViaRekick
721			}
722			c.metrics.recordCleared(ctx, via)
723		}
724	}

726	// truncateError renders an error for the index, capped so a pathological message
727	// can't bloat the KV value.
728	func truncateError(err error) string {
729		if err == nil {
730			return ""
731		}
732		const max = 1024
733		s := err.Error()
734		if len(s) > max {
735			return s[:max]
736		}
737		return s
738	}

740	// inProgressMsg is the subset of *nats.Msg used by the in-progress extender.
741	// A tiny interface seam so the loop is unit-testable without a live JetStream
742	// subscription. Signature mirrors *nats.Msg.InProgress (variadic AckOpt) so
743	// the concrete type satisfies the interface implicitly.
744	type inProgressMsg interface {
745		InProgress(opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
746	}
747	
748	// startInProgressExtender periodically calls msg.InProgress() to push back the
749	// JetStream redelivery deadline while a long-running operation (a git sync)
750	// is still in flight. Returns a stop function that cancels the loop and blocks
751	// until the goroutine has exited — so a defer-stop won't leak the goroutine.
752	//
753	// InProgress() errors are logged and swallowed: a transient extend failure
754	// shouldn't kill an otherwise healthy job. Worst case the sync exceeds
755	// AckWait without a successful extend and JetStream redelivers — the same
756	// redelivery path that already exists today.
757	func startInProgressExtender(ctx context.Context, msg inProgressMsg, interval time.Duration) (stop func()) {
758		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
759		done := make(chan struct{})
760		go func() {
761			defer close(done)
762			ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
763			defer ticker.Stop()
764			for {
765				select {
766				case <-ctx.Done():
767					return
768				case <-ticker.C:
769					if err := msg.InProgress(); err != nil {
770						slog.WarnContext(ctx, "InProgress extend failed", slog.Any("error", err))
771					}
772				}
773			}
774		}()
775		return func() {
776			cancel()
777			<-done
778		}
779	}

29	const (
30		consumerBackoffInit = 1 * time.Second
31		consumerBackoffMax  = 30 * time.Second
32	
33		// consumerFailureDelay is the flat delay between redeliveries on a transient
34		// failure (network error or 5xx), requested explicitly via msg.NakWithDelay
35		// (a bare Nak() does NOT honor a delay — the server redelivers immediately).
36		// Matches cmd/fanout: a short, fixed in-stream retry rather than an
37		// escalating backoff. The DLQ captures the delivery on MaxDeliver exhaustion
38		// for replay once entire-web recovers.
39		consumerFailureDelay = 30 * time.Second
40	
41		// consumerMaxDeliver bounds redelivery: first attempt + 7 retries. Kept at 8
42		// (the value the live durable was created with) so this change reconciles onto
43		// the existing JetStream consumer without a delete-and-recreate: the client's
44		// checkConfig rejects a MaxDeliver mismatch, and dropping nats.BackOff is
45		// tolerated (BackOff is not part of that comparison).
46		consumerMaxDeliver = 8
47	
48		// consumerAckWait is the redelivery backstop when a pod dies mid-dispatch
49		// without responding (no Ack/Nak/Term). The forward POST is fast, so a short
50		// window is safe. No nats.BackOff is set, so this is a free choice — not
51		// clamped to a schedule.
52		consumerAckWait = 30 * time.Second
53	
54		// consumerInactiveThreshold lets the SERVER reap this durable after 72h
55		// without a pull request. webhooks_github_v1 is interest-retention: an
56		// abandoned durable pins every subsequent delivery for ALL consumers
57		// until the stream's maxAge/maxBytes wall — the 2026-06-01 incident.
58		// 72h sits under the stream's 96h maxAge; an app deliberately down
59		// longer loses its cursor and re-consumes what is still retained on
60		// return. Reconciled onto the existing durable in run() — the client's
61		// checkConfig does not compare this field, so PullSubscribe alone would
62		// silently leave the live consumer without it.
63		consumerInactiveThreshold = 72 * time.Hour
64	)

66	const tracerName = "webhook-forwarder"

68	// githubSignatureHeader is the HMAC header GitHub sends and webhook-ingest both
69	// verifies (rejecting unsigned deliveries with 403) and replays verbatim into the
70	// envelope (cmd/webhook-ingest/forward.go). Its presence therefore marks a genuine
71	// GitHub-originated delivery; an envelope without it was published straight onto
72	// webhooks_github_v1 by another producer and is not forwardable to entire-web.
73	const githubSignatureHeader = "X-Hub-Signature-256"

75	type forwarder struct {
76		js        nats.JetStreamContext
77		client    *http.Client
78		metrics   *forwarderMetrics
79		targetURL string
80		durable   string
81		subject   string
82		// health drives the severity of subscribe/fetch failure logs: recoverable
83		// interruptions log at warn until the loop goes too long without progress.
84		health natslog.Health
85		// dlq captures deliveries this forwarder dead-letters (Term on a permanent
86		// reject, or MaxDeliver-exhaustion on a sustained entire-web outage) so a
87		// non-reconstructible webhook isn't lost. nil disables capture (behavior then
88		// identical to before) — wired only when ENTIRE_WEBHOOK_DLQ_ENABLED is set, so
89		// this ships ahead of the fleet stream + PUBLISH grant.
90		dlq *webhookdlq.Publisher
91	
92		// subscribed tracks whether the forwarder currently holds a live JetStream
93		// pull subscription. /readyz consults it so a pod that can dial NATS but
94		// cannot PullSubscribe (a consumer-config mismatch, a perm reject) is reported
95		// NotReady instead of silently forwarding nothing. Mirrors cmd/fanout.
96		subscribed atomic.Bool
97	}
98	
99	// Ready reports whether the forwarder currently holds a live JetStream pull
100	// subscription. Cleared during the backoff window between failed subscribes.
101	func (f *forwarder) Ready() bool {
102		return f.subscribed.Load()
103	}
104	
105	// ensureInactiveThreshold reconciles consumerInactiveThreshold onto an
106	// already-existing durable before the subscribe — PullSubscribe binds to an
107	// existing consumer and silently ignores the requested InactiveThreshold
108	// (checkConfig does not compare it), so without this the live fleet would
109	// never pick it up. Mirrors fanoutengine.(*Consumer).ensureInactiveThreshold.
110	// Best-effort: on any error the subscribe proceeds and the next run loop
111	// iteration retries.
112	func (f *forwarder) ensureInactiveThreshold() {
113		info, err := f.js.ConsumerInfo(webhookevents.StreamName, f.durable)
114		if err != nil {
115			if !errors.Is(err, nats.ErrConsumerNotFound) && !errors.Is(err, nats.ErrStreamNotFound) {
116				slog.Warn("InactiveThreshold reconcile: consumer lookup failed; proceeding without update",
117					slog.String("durable", f.durable), slog.Any("error", err))
118			}
119			return
120		}
121		if info.Config.InactiveThreshold == consumerInactiveThreshold {
122			return
123		}
124		updated := info.Config
125		updated.InactiveThreshold = consumerInactiveThreshold
126		if _, err := f.js.UpdateConsumer(webhookevents.StreamName, &updated); err != nil {
127			slog.Warn("InactiveThreshold reconcile: consumer update failed; proceeding without update",
128				slog.String("durable", f.durable), slog.Any("error", err))
129			return
130		}
131		slog.Info("InactiveThreshold reconciled onto existing durable",
132			slog.String("durable", f.durable), slog.Duration("inactive_threshold", consumerInactiveThreshold))
133	}
134	
135	func (f *forwarder) run(ctx context.Context) {
136		backoff := consumerBackoffInit
137		for {
138			f.subscribed.Store(false)
139			f.ensureInactiveThreshold()
140			sub, err := f.js.PullSubscribe(f.subject, f.durable,
141				nats.ManualAck(),
142				nats.AckWait(consumerAckWait),
143				nats.MaxDeliver(consumerMaxDeliver),
144				nats.InactiveThreshold(consumerInactiveThreshold),
145			)
146			if err != nil {
147				f.health.SubscribeErr(ctx, "Subscribe failed", err,
148					slog.String("subject", f.subject),
149					slog.String("durable", f.durable),
150				)
151				select {
152				case <-ctx.Done():
153					return
154				case <-time.After(backoff):
155					backoff = minDuration(backoff*2, consumerBackoffMax)
156					continue
157				}
158			}
159			backoff = consumerBackoffInit
160			f.subscribed.Store(true)
161			slog.Info("Subscribed", slog.String("subject", f.subject), slog.String("durable", f.durable))
162	
163			f.consumeLoop(ctx, sub)
164			f.subscribed.Store(false)
165	
166			if ctx.Err() != nil {
167				return
168			}
169		}
170	}
171	
172	func (f *forwarder) consumeLoop(ctx context.Context, sub *nats.Subscription) {
173		for {
174			if ctx.Err() != nil {
175				return
176			}
177			msgs, err := sub.Fetch(1, nats.MaxWait(5*time.Second))
178			if err != nil {
179				if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) {
180					// An idle poll is progress: connected, stream merely quiet.
181					f.health.Recovered()
182					continue
183				}
184				if nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) {
185					return
186				}
187				f.health.Err(ctx, "Fetch error", err)
188				return
189			}
190			f.health.Recovered()
191			for _, msg := range msgs {
192				f.handleMessage(ctx, msg)
193			}
194		}
195	}

197	func (f *forwarder) handleMessage(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
198		ctx = natsmsg.Extract(ctx, msg)
199		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "webhook.forward.dispatch",
200			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindConsumer),
201			trace.WithAttributes(
202				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
203				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "receive"),
204				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", msg.Subject),
205			),
206		)
207		defer span.End()
208	
209		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
210			span.SetAttributes(
211				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(meta.Sequence.Stream)),
212				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.delivery_count", int64(meta.NumDelivered)),
213			)
214		}
215	
216		f.dispatch(ctx, span, msg)
217	}

219	// ackableMsg is the disposition subset of *nats.Msg the panic handler needs; a
220	// seam so handlePanic is unit-testable without a live JetStream subscription.
221	type ackableMsg interface {
222		Ack(opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
223		Nak(opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
224		NakWithDelay(delay time.Duration, opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
225		Term(opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
226	}
227	
228	// handlePanic disposes of a delivery whose handler panicked. It Naks (not
229	// Terms) so the only durable copy of the webhook isn't permanently dropped on a
230	// first panic: redelivery is bounded by MaxDeliver, so a transient cause recovers
231	// on a later delivery and a deterministic one ages out of the stream — both
232	// WITHOUT crashing the process. It Naks WITH a delay (consumerFailureDelay): a
233	// bare Nak() would redeliver immediately and burn through MaxDeliver in
234	// milliseconds across replicas. Asymmetry with the transient path, by design: a
235	// panic on the FINAL delivery is Nak'd and dropped at MaxDeliver with NO DLQ
236	// capture — a panic is a deterministic code bug, not a recoverable webhook, so
237	// replay can't fix it. The stack is logged once here so the poison-pill payload
238	// is still diagnosable; the span carries entire.handler.panicked for queries.
239	func (f *forwarder) handlePanic(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg ackableMsg, recovered any) {
240		err := fmt.Errorf("panic recovered in forwarder handler: %v", recovered)
241		span.RecordError(err)
242		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "handler panic")
243		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.handler.panicked", true))
244		slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Recovered panic in forwarder handler; naking delivery (bounded by MaxDeliver)",
245			slog.Any("panic", recovered),
246			slog.String("stack", string(debug.Stack())),
247		)
248		f.metrics.recordPanic(ctx)
249		_ = msg.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
250	}
251	
252	// dispatch is the per-message handler. It unmarshals, POSTs to entire-web,
253	// and ack/nak/term-s based on the response. Exposed for testing.
254	func (f *forwarder) dispatch(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg *nats.Msg) {
255		// A panic here (a nil deref, a bug in the HTTP path on a pathological body)
256		// must NOT unwind into the consume goroutine: that crashes the process, and
257		// because the message was never acked JetStream redelivers it — so every
258		// replica that picks it up crashes in turn, turning one poison-pill delivery
259		// into a cluster-wide crash-loop. Recover and Nak instead.
260		defer func() {
261			if r := recover(); r != nil {
262				f.handlePanic(ctx, span, msg, r)
263			}
264		}()
265	
266		forwarded, err := webhookevents.Unmarshal(msg.Data)
267		if err != nil {
268			// Malformed payload — broker routed something we cannot interpret.
269			// Terminate without redelivery; the dropped message is searchable in
270			// Honeycomb via the span error.
271			span.RecordError(err)
272			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "unmarshal forwarded webhook")
273			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
274			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Bad forwarded webhook, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
275			f.deadLetter(ctx, span, webhookdlq.ReasonBadEnvelope, msg, nil, numDelivered(msg), err)
276			f.metrics.recordForward(ctx, eventUnknown, forwardOutcomeTerm, forwardReasonBadEnvelope)
277			_ = msg.Term()
278			return
279		}
280		span.SetAttributes(
281			attribute.String("github.delivery_id", forwarded.DeliveryID),
282			attribute.String("github.event", forwarded.Event),
283		)
284	
285		// A well-formed envelope with no X-Hub-Signature-256 is not a GitHub delivery:
286		// ingest only publishes deliveries whose signature it verified, and replays that
287		// header verbatim. An unsigned envelope was published straight onto the stream by
288		// another producer (e.g. entire-core's "mirror resync", which re-triggers fanout
289		// with a stub push). The sibling fanout consumer handles those; forwarding one to
290		// entire-web only earns a guaranteed 4xx that dead-letters as noise. Ack without
291		// forwarding — it is not a drop (nothing was ever meant for entire-web here, so
292		// there is nothing to preserve or replay).
293		if !hasGitHubSignature(forwarded.Headers) {
294			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.forward.skipped", true))
295			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Skipping unsigned (non-GitHub) delivery; not forwarding",
296				slog.String("delivery_id", forwarded.DeliveryID),
297				slog.String("event", forwarded.Event))
298			f.metrics.recordForward(ctx, forwarded.Event, forwardOutcomeSkip, forwardReasonUnsigned)
299			_ = msg.Ack()
300			return
301		}
302	
303		deliveries := numDelivered(msg)
304	
305		status, err := f.forward(ctx, forwarded)
306		if err != nil {
307			span.RecordError(err)
308			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "forward request")
309			f.nakOrDeadLetter(ctx, span, msg, forwarded, deliveries, forwardReasonNetwork, err)
310			return
311		}
312		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int("http.response.status_code", status))
313	
314		switch {
315		case status >= 200 && status < 300:
316			f.metrics.recordForward(ctx, forwarded.Event, forwardOutcomeAck, "")
317			_ = msg.Ack()
318			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Forwarded",
319				slog.String("delivery_id", forwarded.DeliveryID),
320				slog.String("event", forwarded.Event),
321				slog.Int("http.status_code", status))
322		case status == http.StatusUnauthorized, status == http.StatusForbidden:
323			// Auth / authz problem — entire-web rejected the request (e.g. the
324			// shared webhook secret drifted, or its request gating kicked in).
325			// Either way it's a config issue; retrying without operator action
326			// just burns deliveries. Dead-letter so the delivery survives the
327			// config fix for replay.
328			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "auth rejected")
329			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
330			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Forward auth rejected; terminating",
331				slog.String("delivery_id", forwarded.DeliveryID),
332				slog.Int("http.status_code", status))
333			f.deadLetter(ctx, span, webhookdlq.ReasonAuth, msg, &forwarded, deliveries, fmt.Errorf("entire-web returned %d", status))
334			f.metrics.recordForward(ctx, forwarded.Event, forwardOutcomeTerm, forwardReasonAuth)
335			_ = msg.Term()
336		case status >= 400 && status < 500:
337			// Other 4xx — entire-web rejected the body. Retry won't fix it, but
338			// preserve it for inspection (the body may reveal why entire-web 4xx'd).
339			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, fmt.Sprintf("client error %d", status))
340			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
341			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Forward rejected with 4xx; terminating",
342				slog.String("delivery_id", forwarded.DeliveryID),
343				slog.Int("http.status_code", status))
344			f.deadLetter(ctx, span, webhookdlq.ReasonClientError, msg, &forwarded, deliveries, fmt.Errorf("entire-web returned %d", status))
345			f.metrics.recordForward(ctx, forwarded.Event, forwardOutcomeTerm, forwardReasonClientError)
346			_ = msg.Term()
347		default:
348			// 5xx or unexpected status — transient on entire-web's side.
349			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, fmt.Sprintf("server error %d", status))
350			f.nakOrDeadLetter(ctx, span, msg, forwarded, deliveries, forwardReasonServerError, fmt.Errorf("entire-web returned %d", status))
351		}
352	}
353	
354	// nakOrDeadLetter disposes a transient forward failure (network error or 5xx).
355	// Normally it NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay) for JetStream redelivery on a
356	// flat delay (a bare Nak would redeliver immediately). On the FINAL delivery a
357	// Nak is dropped silently at MaxDeliver, so — when DLQ capture is enabled — it
358	// dead-letters the webhook and Terms instead, preserving the only copy for replay
359	// once entire-web recovers. reason is the transient class for the Nak metric
360	// (network|server_error). deliveries is threaded in (rather than read from msg
361	// here) so the decision is unit-testable without a live JetStream subscription,
362	// matching the forwarder's existing test seams.
363	func (f *forwarder) nakOrDeadLetter(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg *nats.Msg, fw webhookevents.ForwardedWebhook, deliveries int, reason string, cause error) {
364		if f.dlq != nil && deliveries >= consumerMaxDeliver {
365			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Forward failed; deliveries exhausted, dead-lettering",
366				slog.String("delivery_id", fw.DeliveryID), slog.String("event", fw.Event), slog.Any("error", cause))
367			f.deadLetter(ctx, span, webhookdlq.ReasonMaxDeliveries, msg, &fw, deliveries, cause)
368			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
369			f.metrics.recordForward(ctx, fw.Event, forwardOutcomeTerm, forwardReasonExhausted)
370			_ = msg.Term()
371			return
372		}
373		slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Forward failed; will redeliver",
374			slog.String("delivery_id", fw.DeliveryID), slog.String("event", fw.Event),
375			slog.Int("delivery", deliveries), slog.Duration("redeliver_in", consumerFailureDelay), slog.Any("error", cause))
376		f.metrics.recordForward(ctx, fw.Event, forwardOutcomeNak, reason)
377		_ = msg.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
378	}
379	
380	// deadLetter best-effort captures a dead-lettered delivery to the DLQ. No-op
381	// when capture is disabled (f.dlq == nil). On a publish failure it fails open —
382	// logs + a span event, and the caller Terms anyway — because the failure is
383	// permanent (replay can't fix the cause) or the deliveries are exhausted, so
384	// holding the message only re-runs doomed work. The drop-with-no-copy is
385	// surfaced by webhook.dlq.published{outcome=error}. fw is nil for a delivery
386	// whose envelope didn't parse (the raw bytes are still preserved for triage).
387	func (f *forwarder) deadLetter(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, reason string, msg *nats.Msg, fw *webhookevents.ForwardedWebhook, deliveries int, cause error) {
388		if f.dlq == nil {
389			return
390		}
391		dl := webhookdlq.DeadLetter{
392			Source:          webhookdlq.SourceForwarder,
393			Reason:          reason,
394			OriginalSubject: msg.Subject,
395			Envelope:        msg.Data,
396			Deliveries:      deliveries,
397			DeadLetteredAt:  time.Now(),
398		}
399		if cause != nil {
400			dl.LastError = cause.Error()
401		}
402		if fw != nil {
403			dl.DeliveryID = fw.DeliveryID
404			dl.Event = fw.Event
405		}
406		if err := f.dlq.Publish(ctx, dl); err != nil {
407			span.AddEvent("webhook.dlq.publish_failed")
408			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Failed to capture dead-lettered webhook; terminating anyway (fail open)",
409				slog.String("reason", reason), slog.Any("error", err))
410		}
411	}
412	
413	// hasGitHubSignature reports whether the forwarded envelope carries a non-empty
414	// X-Hub-Signature-256 header — the marker of a genuine GitHub delivery (see the
415	// header constant). Case-insensitive: the envelope's header-map key is
416	// producer-set and not guaranteed to be canonicalized. A nil/empty map returns
417	// false, so a directly-published headerless event is treated as unsigned.
418	func hasGitHubSignature(headers map[string]string) bool {
419		for k, v := range headers {
420			if v != "" && strings.EqualFold(k, githubSignatureHeader) {
421				return true
422			}
423		}
424		return false
425	}
426	
427	// numDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count, or 0 if metadata is
428	// unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test message with no JetStream reply subject).
429	func numDelivered(msg *nats.Msg) int {
430		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
431			return int(meta.NumDelivered)
432		}
433		return 0
434	}
435	
436	// forward issues the POST to entire-web. Returns the response status code.
437	// A non-nil error means the request never produced a response (network /
438	// timeout) and the caller should treat it as transient.
439	func (f *forwarder) forward(ctx context.Context, w webhookevents.ForwardedWebhook) (int, error) {
440		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, f.targetURL, bytes.NewReader(w.Body))
441		if err != nil {
442			return 0, fmt.Errorf("build request: %w", err)
443		}
444		// Replay GH headers verbatim — including X-Hub-Signature-256 — so the
445		// downstream (entire-web) verifies HMAC against the same secret it has
446		// always used. mirror-pipeline does not add its own auth; the request is
447		// indistinguishable from a direct GitHub delivery.
448		for k, v := range w.Headers {
449			req.Header.Set(k, v)
450		}
451		if req.Header.Get("Content-Type") == "" {
452			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
453		}
454	
455		resp, err := f.client.Do(req)
456		if err != nil {
457			return 0, err
458		}
459		defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
460		// Drain the body so the connection can be reused.
461		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)
462		return resp.StatusCode, nil
463	}
464	
465	func minDuration(a, b time.Duration) time.Duration {
466		if a < b {
467			return a
468		}
469		return b
470	}

27	const (
28		// lifecycleStream is the JetStream stream carrying resource_lifecycle_v1 on
29		// every cell. Provisioned declaratively in fleet (apps/nats-streams) —
30		// meta-fanout neither creates nor reconciles it, it only consumes the local
31		// copy and re-publishes into each remote cell's copy.
32		lifecycleStream = "resource_lifecycle_v1"
33	
34		// lifecycleSubjectFilter binds the consumer to the whole stream. meta-fanout
35		// is a dumb cross-region pipe for resource_lifecycle_v1: it fans every
36		// subtype (github_handle.*, verified_email.*, and the org/project/repo
37		// binding events that share the bus) and leaves subtype filtering to the
38		// per-cell consumers downstream.
39		lifecycleSubjectFilter = lifecycleStream + ".>"
40	
41		// lifecycleDurable is meta-fanout's durable on the LOCAL
42		// resource_lifecycle_v1 stream — distinct from the github_meta webhook and
43		// backfill durables so the three drain independently. Overridable via env for
44		// non-prod / migration.
45		lifecycleDurable = "meta-fanout-lifecycle"
46	
47		// lifecyclePublishAckWait bounds the synchronous pub-ack on each remote
48		// region's PublishMsg (the shared natspub.AckWait, so the lifecycle fan
49		// can't drift from the job publishers). A publish routed to a reconnecting
50		// region becomes a bounded error → consumer Nak → JetStream redelivery,
51		// instead of parking in the client's reconnect buffer and stalling the
52		// serial consume loop until the region returns.
53		lifecyclePublishAckWait = natspub.AckWait
54	
55		// lifecycleFannedByHeader marks a resource_lifecycle_v1 event as an
56		// already-fanned cross-region copy. publishOne stamps it (value = the
57		// fanning cell's cluster id) on every copy it emits; dispatch skips
58		// re-fanning any event that already carries it. That makes the fan exactly
59		// one generation deep: an event fanned US→EU is not re-fanned by EU back to
60		// US or on to AP, so a cross-region echo loop is structurally impossible at
61		// any lag — independent of the destination dedup window (COR-902). The value
62		// is for debuggability (which cell exported it); the guard keys on presence.
63		// Carried verbatim across hops like any user header, so once stamped it stays
64		// stamped.
65		lifecycleFannedByHeader = "Entire-Lifecycle-Fanned-By"
66	)

68	// lifecycleFanout re-publishes one resource_lifecycle_v1 event into the local
69	// resource_lifecycle_v1 stream of every REMOTE region, subject and payload
70	// verbatim.
71	//
72	// The local cell is deliberately not a target: entire-core already emitted the
73	// event into the local stream (that is what this consumer reads), so publishing
74	// it back would feed the consumer its own output — an infinite loop, since here
75	// the source and target stream are the same (unlike github_meta_v1, whose
76	// source is the separate webhooks_github_v1 stream). meta-fanout's only job is
77	// to carry the event to the OTHER cells. With no remotes configured
78	// (single-region mode) the fan is a no-op and the delivery simply Acks.
79	type lifecycleFanout struct {
80		remotes map[string]metajobs.JetStreamPublisher // cluster_id → remote JetStream
81	
82		// localClusterID is this cell's cluster id (FANOUT_LOCAL_CLUSTER_ID). It is
83		// stamped as the lifecycleFannedByHeader value on every fanned copy so the
84		// one-generation guard in dispatch can suppress echoes. Empty only in
85		// single-region mode, where remotes is also empty and the fan never runs.
86		localClusterID string
87	}
88	
89	// fan publishes (subject, data) into every remote region. Regions are
90	// independent: a failure on one (a region momentarily disconnected) must not
91	// stop the others, so we attempt all and return a non-nil error if any failed
92	// — the caller Naks and the whole event rides JetStream redelivery; the regions
93	// that already accepted it re-publish idempotently (same Nats-Msg-Id within the
94	// dedup window).
95	func (f *lifecycleFanout) fan(ctx context.Context, subject, msgID string, data []byte, srcHeader nats.Header) error {
96		span := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)
97	
98		var failed []string
99		var firstErr error
100		for _, clusterID := range f.sortedClusters() {
101			if err := f.publishOne(ctx, f.remotes[clusterID], subject, msgID, data, srcHeader); err != nil {
102				failed = append(failed, clusterID)
103				if firstErr == nil {
104					firstErr = err
105				}
106				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Lifecycle fan failed for region; continuing with remaining regions",
107					slog.String("subject", subject),
108					slog.String("cluster_id", clusterID),
109					slog.Any("error", err))
110			}
111		}
112	
113		span.SetAttributes(
114			attribute.Int("entire.fanout.regions", len(f.remotes)),
115			attribute.Int("entire.fanout.regions_failed", len(failed)),
116		)
117		if len(failed) > 0 {
118			span.SetAttributes(attribute.StringSlice("entire.fanout.failed_cluster_ids", failed))
119			return fmt.Errorf("lifecycle fan failed for %d of %d regions (clusters: %v): %w",
120				len(failed), len(f.remotes), failed, firstErr)
121		}
122		return nil
123	}

125	// publishOne re-publishes the event into one remote region's stream. The source
126	// headers are carried verbatim (preserving the dedup Nats-Msg-Id) on a private
127	// copy per region, then this publish's trace context is injected so the
128	// downstream consumer span parents to meta-fanout rather than the original
129	// producer.
130	func (f *lifecycleFanout) publishOne(ctx context.Context, js metajobs.JetStreamPublisher, subject, msgID string, data []byte, srcHeader nats.Header) error {
131		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "resource_lifecycle.fan",
132			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer),
133			trace.WithAttributes(
134				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
135				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "publish"),
136				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", subject),
137			),
138		)
139		defer span.End()
140	
141		msg := &nats.Msg{
142			Subject: subject,
143			Data:    data,
144			Header:  cloneHeader(srcHeader),
145		}
146		// Mark this copy as fanned so the destination cell does not re-export it
147		// (see dispatch). cloneHeader gave us a private copy, so this never mutates
148		// the shared source header.
149		msg.Header.Set(lifecycleFannedByHeader, f.localClusterID)
150		if msgID != "" {
151			msg.Header.Set(metajobs.NatsMsgIDHeader, msgID)
152			span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", msgID))
153		}
154		natsmsg.Inject(ctx, msg)
155	
156		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, lifecyclePublishAckWait)
157		defer cancel()
158		ack, err := js.PublishMsg(pubCtx, msg)
159		if err != nil {
160			span.RecordError(err)
161			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "nats publish")
162			return fmt.Errorf("publish lifecycle event: %w", err)
163		}
164		span.SetAttributes(
165			attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(ack.Sequence)),
166			attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
167		)
168		return nil
169	}

171	func (f *lifecycleFanout) sortedClusters() []string {
172		out := make([]string, 0, len(f.remotes))
173		for cid := range f.remotes {
174			out = append(out, cid)
175		}
176		sort.Strings(out)
177		return out
178	}

180	// lifecycleConsumer drains the LOCAL resource_lifecycle_v1 stream and fans each
181	// event cross-region. Its own durable keeps it isolated from the github_meta
182	// webhook and backfill consumers on their own streams. The ack discipline
183	// mirrors the github_meta consumer: explicit ManualAck with a bounded AckWait
184	// and MaxDeliver, NakWithDelay on a transient fan failure, Ack on success.
185	// There is no Term path — the event is republished verbatim, so nothing about
186	// it can be permanently unprocessable.
187	type lifecycleConsumer struct {
188		js      nats.JetStreamContext
189		fanout  *lifecycleFanout
190		metrics *metaFanoutMetrics
191		durable string
192		subject string
193		// health drives the severity of subscribe/fetch failure logs: recoverable
194		// interruptions log at warn until the loop goes too long without progress.
195		health natslog.Health
196	
197		// enqueuer + resolver drive the additive mirror.created → github_meta seed
198		// (COR-717). Both nil leaves the consumer a pure cross-region fan (its
199		// original behavior), so fan-only tests need not wire them.
200		enqueuer backfillEnqueuer
201		resolver mirrorResolver
202	
203		// subscribed mirrors the github_meta consumer's /readyz gate: a pod that can
204		// dial NATS but cannot PullSubscribe (auth/perm/durable-config problem) is
205		// reported NotReady instead of silently looping on backoff.
206		subscribed atomic.Bool
207	}
208	
209	// Ready returns true while the consumer holds a live pull subscription.
210	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) Ready() bool { return c.subscribed.Load() }
211	
212	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) run(ctx context.Context) {
213		backoff := consumerBackoffInit
214		for {
215			c.subscribed.Store(false)
216			sub, err := c.js.PullSubscribe(c.subject, c.durable,
217				nats.ManualAck(),
218				nats.AckWait(consumerAckWait),
219				nats.MaxDeliver(consumerMaxDeliver),
220			)
221			if err != nil {
222				c.health.SubscribeErr(ctx, "Lifecycle subscribe failed", err,
223					slog.String("subject", c.subject), slog.String("durable", c.durable))
224				select {
225				case <-ctx.Done():
226					return
227				case <-time.After(backoff):
228					backoff = min(backoff*2, consumerBackoffMax)
229					continue
230				}
231			}
232			backoff = consumerBackoffInit
233			c.subscribed.Store(true)
234			slog.Info("Lifecycle subscribed", slog.String("subject", c.subject), slog.String("durable", c.durable))
235	
236			c.consumeLoop(ctx, sub)
237			c.subscribed.Store(false)
238	
239			if ctx.Err() != nil {
240				return
241			}
242		}
243	}
244	
245	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) consumeLoop(ctx context.Context, sub *nats.Subscription) {
246		for {
247			if ctx.Err() != nil {
248				return
249			}
250			msgs, err := sub.Fetch(1, nats.MaxWait(5*time.Second))
251			if err != nil {
252				if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) {
253					// An idle poll is progress: connected, stream merely quiet.
254					c.health.Recovered()
255					continue
256				}
257				// This loop lacked the shutdown guard its siblings carry, so a
258				// clean teardown surfaced as a fault here.
259				if nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) {
260					return
261				}
262				c.health.Err(ctx, "Lifecycle fetch error", err)
263				return
264			}
265			c.health.Recovered()
266			for _, msg := range msgs {
267				c.handleMessage(ctx, msg)
268			}
269		}
270	}
271	
272	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) handleMessage(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
273		ctx = natsmsg.Extract(ctx, msg)
274		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "meta_fanout.lifecycle_fan",
275			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindConsumer),
276			trace.WithAttributes(
277				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
278				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "receive"),
279				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", msg.Subject),
280			),
281		)
282		defer span.End()
283	
284		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
285			span.SetAttributes(
286				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(meta.Sequence.Stream)),
287				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.delivery_count", int64(meta.NumDelivered)),
288			)
289		}
290	
291		c.dispatch(ctx, span, msg.Subject, msg.Data, msg.Header, msg)
292	}
293	
294	// dispatch is the per-message handler. Exposed so tests can drive the fan + ack
295	// behavior directly with a fake ackableMsg, no live JetStream needed.
296	func (c *lifecycleConsumer) dispatch(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, subject string, data []byte, header nats.Header, msg ackableMsg) {
297		// A panic anywhere below must NOT unwind into the consume goroutine: that
298		// crashes the process, and because the message was never acked JetStream
299		// redelivers it — so every replica that picks it up crashes in turn, turning
300		// one poison-pill delivery into a cluster-wide crash-loop. Recover and Nak
301		// (bounded by MaxDeliver) instead.
302		defer func() {
303			if r := recover(); r != nil {
304				err := fmt.Errorf("panic recovered in lifecycle handler: %v", r)
305				span.RecordError(err)
306				span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "handler panic")
307				span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.handler.panicked", true))
308				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Recovered panic in lifecycle handler; naking delivery (bounded by MaxDeliver)",
309					slog.Any("panic", r), slog.String("stack", string(debug.Stack())))
310				c.metrics.recordPanic(ctx)
311				_ = msg.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
312			}
313		}()
314	
315		span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.lifecycle.subject", subject))
316	
317		// Additive to the verbatim fan: on a mirror.created, enqueue a github_meta
318		// backfill so a new mirror gets its display metadata without a webhook or a
319		// manual run (COR-717). Best-effort by design — it never touches the ack
320		// disposition below, which stays governed solely by the fan. Run before the
321		// fan so a delivery the fan will Nak (remote region down) still seeds; the
322		// backfill dedup id makes the redelivery idempotent.
323		c.maybeSeedMirrorMeta(ctx, span, subject, data)
324	
325		// One-generation fan (COR-902): if this event already carries the fanned-by
326		// marker it is a cross-region copy some cell exported (possibly ours, hops
327		// ago), so do NOT re-export it — re-fanning imported copies is exactly the
328		// echo that recirculated at ~16.5/s across all cells. Ack and stop here. This
329		// runs AFTER maybeSeedMirrorMeta on purpose: a foreign-origin mirror.created
330		// reaches US only as a fanned copy and US is where the github_meta seed runs
331		// (COR-717), so the seed must still fire for marked messages. And it does not
332		// affect downstream consumers — the event is already in this cell's stream
333		// where entire-api's repolifecycle / mirror-lifecycle / settings consumers
334		// read it (COR-901); only the re-EXPORT is suppressed.
335		if _, marked := header[lifecycleFannedByHeader]; marked {
336			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.lifecycle.fanned_in", true))
337			c.metrics.recordLifecycleFan(ctx, dispatchOutcomeSkippedForeign)
338			_ = msg.Ack()
339			return
340		}
341	
342		if err := c.fanout.fan(ctx, subject, lifecycleMsgID(header, msg), data, header); err != nil {
343			// A region was unreachable. NakWithDelay so JetStream redelivers after
344			// the flat consumerFailureDelay; acking would drop the only durable copy
345			// of the event before it reached every region. On the final delivery the
346			// Nak is dropped silently at MaxDeliver (no DLQ — the source stream
347			// retains the event and replay is a separate path).
348			span.RecordError(err)
349			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "lifecycle fan")
350			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Lifecycle fan failed; will redeliver",
351				slog.String("subject", subject),
352				slog.Int("delivery", numDelivered(msg)),
353				slog.Duration("redeliver_in", consumerFailureDelay),
354				slog.Any("error", err))
355			c.metrics.recordLifecycleFan(ctx, dispatchOutcomeNak)
356			_ = msg.NakWithDelay(consumerFailureDelay)
357			return
358		}
359	
360		c.metrics.recordLifecycleFan(ctx, dispatchOutcomeAck)
361		_ = msg.Ack()
362		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Fanned lifecycle event", slog.String("subject", subject))
363	}
364	
365	// lifecycleMsgID returns the dedup key carried onto the fanned copies. It
366	// prefers the source event's own Nats-Msg-Id (stable across the source's
367	// redeliveries and semantically the same logical event), falling back to the
368	// source stream + sequence (also stable for a given stored message) so a
369	// republish always collapses on the remote dedup window. Empty only for a
370	// synthetic message with neither, in which case dedup is simply not applied.
371	func lifecycleMsgID(srcHeader nats.Header, msg ackableMsg) string {
372		if srcHeader != nil {
373			if id := srcHeader.Get(metajobs.NatsMsgIDHeader); id != "" {
374				return id
375			}
376		}
377		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
378			return lifecycleStream + ":" + strconv.FormatUint(meta.Sequence.Stream, 10)
379		}
380		return ""
381	}
382	
383	// cloneHeader deep-copies a nats.Header so per-region trace injection does not
384	// mutate the shared source header. A nil source yields an empty, writable map.
385	func cloneHeader(h nats.Header) nats.Header {
386		out := make(nats.Header, len(h))
387		for k, v := range h {
388			out[k] = append([]string(nil), v...)
389		}
390		return out
391	}

8		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
