11		"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/pkg/webhookevents"
12	)
13	
14	// Retry envelope, mirroring cmd/fanout: a flat NakWithDelay redelivery (no
15	// escalating BackOff) bounded by MaxDeliver, with a short AckWait backstop for
16	// a pod that dies mid-dispatch. meta-fanout dispatch (unmarshal → route →
17	// publish) is sub-second, so the short windows are safe. Shared by the engine
18	// consumers (the live webhook dispatcher and the github_meta backfill, which
19	// gets the engine's Config.TermOnExhaustion work-queue disposition) and the
20	// still-hand-rolled github_pr backfill + lifecycle consumers. The Backoff*
21	// constants are now only the hand-rolled consumers' subscribe-retry cadence
22	// (the engine has its own internal backoff).
23	const (
24		consumerBackoffInit = 1 * time.Second
25		consumerBackoffMax  = 30 * time.Second
26	
27		// consumerFailureDelay is the flat delay between redeliveries on a
28		// transient failure, requested via msg.NakWithDelay (a bare Nak() does NOT
29		// honor a delay — the server redelivers immediately).
30		consumerFailureDelay = 30 * time.Second
31	
32		// consumerMaxDeliver bounds redelivery: first attempt + 7 retries.
33		consumerMaxDeliver = 8
34	
35		// consumerAckWait is the redelivery backstop when a pod dies mid-dispatch
36		// without responding (no Ack/Nak/Term).
37		consumerAckWait = 30 * time.Second
38	
39		// consumerInactiveThreshold lets the SERVER reap the LIVE webhook durable
40		// after 72h without a pull request — webhooks_github_v1 is
41		// interest-retention, so an abandoned durable pins every subsequent
42		// delivery for all consumers until the stream's maxAge/maxBytes wall (the
43		// 2026-06-01 incident). 72h sits under the stream's 96h maxAge. NOT
44		// applied to the backfill durables: their work-queue streams pin nothing
45		// when idle, and sitting idle between backfill runs is their normal
46		// state. See fanoutengine.Config.InactiveThreshold.
47		consumerInactiveThreshold = 72 * time.Hour
48	)
49	
50	const tracerName = "meta-fanout"
51	
52	// newConsumer wires the meta dispatcher (star/fork/repository → github_meta,
53	// pull_request → github_pr) into the shared fanoutengine runtime: the consumer
54	// scaffold (subscribe/backoff loop, Ack/Nak/Term decision tree, panic recovery,
55	// OTel span + trace propagation) lives in the engine; the envelope decode, span
56	// attrs, and metrics are plugged in here. js may be nil when only Dispatch is
57	// exercised (tests). meta-fanout has no nak-reason refinement (no DLQ, no
58	// unmapped-cluster split) so ClassifyNak is omitted.
59	func newConsumer(js nats.JetStreamContext, resolver *metaResolver, regions fanoutengine.Regions, metrics *metaFanoutMetrics, durable, subject string) *fanoutengine.Consumer {
60		return fanoutengine.New(js, webhookDecoder{}, resolver, regions, hooksFor(metrics), fanoutengine.Config{
61			Subject:           subject,
62			Stream:            webhookevents.StreamName,
63			Durable:           durable,
64			Tracer:            tracerName,
65			SpanName:          "meta_fanout.dispatch", // preserve the existing span name verbatim
66			AckWait:           consumerAckWait,
67			MaxDeliver:        consumerMaxDeliver,
68			NakDelay:          consumerFailureDelay,
69			InactiveThreshold: consumerInactiveThreshold,
70			SpanAttrs:         stampGithubSpanAttrs,
71		})
72	}
73	
74	// webhookDecoder turns the raw delivery into the engine envelope by unmarshaling
75	// the ForwardedWebhook contract. A decode failure → Term (bad envelope).

1	// Package fanoutengine is the shared NATS-consumer runtime extracted from the
2	// hand-rolled scaffold that cmd/fanout, cmd/meta-fanout, and cmd/core-fanout
3	// each copy: the subscribe + backoff-retry loop, the Ack/Nak/Term decision
4	// tree, panic recovery, the flat-NakWithDelay retry envelope, OTel span +
5	// trace-context propagation, and /readyz readiness.
6	//
7	// A binary plugs in a Decoder (raw bytes → Envelope) and a Resolver (envelope →
8	// self-describing Routes); the runtime owns everything else, including the
9	// per-region publish + partial-failure aggregation. This is the in-repo
10	// realization of the engine validated by the fanout/ spike — kept on the current
11	// legacy nats.JetStreamContext API and OTel wiring so converting a live binary
12	// is behavior-preserving. The modern jetstream.Consume shape lands when this
13	// graduates to the standalone module.

38	// Subscribe-retry backoff: how long Run waits between attempts to (re-)open the
39	// PullSubscribe, e.g. while the upstream stream is still being ensured at
40	// startup. Distinct from the per-message redelivery delay (Config.NakDelay).
41	const (
42		backoffInit = 1 * time.Second
43		backoffMax  = 30 * time.Second
44	
45		fetchMaxWait = 5 * time.Second

48	// Disposition + term-reason metric strings the runtime emits. Stable wire
49	// contract — dashboards key on these.
50	const (
51		OutcomeAck  = "ack"
52		OutcomeNak  = "nak"
53		OutcomeTerm = "term"
54	
55		ReasonBadEnvelope   = "bad_envelope"   // decode failed — not a valid envelope
56		ReasonInputError    = "input_error"    // envelope ok, body malformed
57		ReasonMaxDeliveries = "max_deliveries" // transient failure exhausted MaxDeliver (DLQ-captured + Term'd)

64	// InputError marks a malformed input body (bad JSON, unparseable identifier) a
65	// Resolver cannot ever process. The runtime Terminates these without

68	// Reason optionally overrides the term-metric reason (default ReasonInputError)
69	// so a consumer can distinguish sub-kinds — e.g. a work-queue job whose source
70	// repo has vanished upstream vs a merely malformed job.

72		Msg    string

76	func (e *InputError) Error() string { return e.Msg }

80

82	// instead of the default ReasonInputError.
83	func InputReason(reason, format string, a ...any) *InputError {
84		return &InputError{Msg: fmt.Sprintf(format, a...), Reason: reason}

88	func AsInputError(err error) (*InputError, bool) {

96	// Envelope is the decoded source envelope handed to a Resolver.

101		Body       []byte
102	}

104	// Decoder turns a raw delivery into an Envelope. A non-nil error → Term

107		Decode(data []byte) (Envelope, error)

110	// Hooks are the metric callbacks. Passed as funcs so a binary's unexported
111	// metric methods can be wired without exporting them. Both are nil-safe.
112	type Hooks struct {
113		RecordDispatch func(ctx context.Context, event, outcome, reason string)
114		RecordPanic    func(ctx context.Context)
115	
116		// Worker-pool + latency instruments (cmd/fanout). All nil-safe; serial
117		// consumers leave them unset. IncActive/DecActive bracket one in-flight
118		// dispatch; RecordFetchBatch reports a non-empty Fetch's size;
119		// RecordDuration reports one dispatch's wall-clock seconds tagged by outcome.
120		IncActive        func(ctx context.Context)
121		DecActive        func(ctx context.Context)
122		RecordFetchBatch func(ctx context.Context, n int)
123		RecordDuration   func(ctx context.Context, outcome string, seconds float64)

126	// Config is the per-consumer wiring.
127	type Config struct {
128		Subject string // subscribe subject/filter, e.g. webhooks.github.v1.push
129		Durable string // pull-consumer durable (distinct per region where applicable)
130		Tracer  string // OTel tracer (instrumentation scope) name, e.g. "core-fanout"
131	
132		// SpanName is the per-message span name. Kept separate from Tracer because
133		// the existing consumers use an underscore form ("core_fanout.dispatch")
134		// distinct from the hyphenated tracer/scope name — trace queries key on it,
135		// so it must be preserved verbatim on conversion. Defaults to
136		// Tracer+".dispatch" when empty.
137		SpanName string
138	
139		// Retry envelope. The runtime applies these to PullSubscribe and to the
140		// per-message NakWithDelay. Callers keep these as their own constants so the
141		// domain-specific invariants (e.g. redelivery-span < dedup-window) stay
142		// testable at the call site.
143		AckWait time.Duration
144		// MaxDeliver is the JetStream delivery-attempt limit. Use -1 for unlimited
145		// transient retries; poison inputs still Term through the decode/InputError
146		// paths independently of this setting.
147		MaxDeliver int
148		NakDelay   time.Duration
149	
150		// InactiveThreshold, when set, has the SERVER delete the durable after
151		// that long without a pull request. On an interest-retention stream
152		// (webhooks_github_v1) an abandoned durable — undeployed or wedged app —
153		// otherwise pins every subsequent matching delivery for ALL consumers
154		// until the stream's maxAge/maxBytes wall (the 2026-06-01 incident);
155		// reaping it releases the backlog. Size it under the stream's maxAge and
156		// well above any deploy gap: an app deliberately down longer loses its
157		// cursor and re-consumes whatever is still retained when it returns
158		// (safe: consumers are idempotent and msg-id-deduped downstream). Leave
159		// unset (0) for work-queue streams, where an idle durable pins nothing.
160		//
161		// Requires Stream: the threshold is reconciled onto an ALREADY-EXISTING
162		// durable via UpdateConsumer before subscribing, because the legacy
163		// PullSubscribe binds to an existing consumer and silently ignores this
164		// field (nats.go checkConfig does not compare it) — without the update,
165		// the option would only take effect on freshly created durables.
166		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
167	
168		// Stream is the JetStream stream the durable lives on. Only needed (and
169		// only used) when InactiveThreshold is set — see above.
170		Stream string
171	
172		// ClassifyNak optionally refines a transient (nak) error into a metric
173		// reason and may annotate the span / log (e.g. an unmapped-cluster misconfig
174		// that won't self-heal). Returns "" for a plain transient outage.
175		ClassifyNak func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, err error) string
176	
177		// SpanAttrs optionally stamps domain attributes from the decoded envelope
178		// (e.g. github.delivery_id / github.event), keeping the runtime domain-free.
179		SpanAttrs func(span trace.Span, env Envelope)
180	
181		// Concurrency / FetchBatch enable a bounded worker pool (cmd/fanout). A
182		// Concurrency of 0 or 1 keeps the strictly-serial Fetch(1) path (the
183		// core-fanout / meta-fanout default, byte-for-byte unchanged). When >1, the
184		// runtime fetches FetchBatch at a time and hands each message to one of
185		// Concurrency workers. FetchBatch MUST be <= Concurrency — the AckWait
186		// correctness bound (JetStream starts a message's AckWait clock when Fetch
187		// delivers it, so an over-large batch leaves the tail aging un-dispatched);
188		// the caller validates this. FetchBatch defaults to 1.
189		Concurrency int
190		FetchBatch  int
191	
192		// DLQ optionally captures dead-lettered deliveries (Term on bad envelope /
193		// input error, or a transient failure exhausting MaxDeliver). nil disables
194		// capture — behavior is then identical to the no-DLQ consumers.
195		DLQ DLQ
196	
197		// TermOnExhaustion makes a transient failure — or a recovered panic — on the
198		// FINAL delivery Term the message (reason=max_deliveries) instead of Nak,
199		// even without a DLQ. For work-queue streams where an un-acked exhausted
200		// message orphans until max_age rather than being redelivered (COR-762);
201		// webhook/durable streams leave it off (Nak, or Term + DLQ capture).
202		TermOnExhaustion bool
203	}

215	// Consumer is the running pull consumer: a Decoder + Resolver driven by the
216	// shared runtime. The Resolver returns Routes and the engine owns the per-region
217	// publish + partial-failure aggregation.
218	type Consumer struct {
219		js       nats.JetStreamContext
220		decoder  Decoder
221		resolver Resolver
222		regions  Regions
223		hooks    Hooks
224		cfg      Config
225		memo     *routeMemo
226	
227		subscribed atomic.Bool
228		// health drives the severity of subscribe/fetch failure logs: recoverable
229		// interruptions log at warn until the loop goes too long without progress.
230		health natslog.Health
231	}
232	
233	// New builds a consumer on the Resolver contract: the Resolver returns Routes and
234	// the engine owns the per-region publish + partial-failure aggregation (publish
235	// all, Nak if any failed, Term + DLQ on exhaustion).
236	func New(js nats.JetStreamContext, decoder Decoder, resolver Resolver, regions Regions, hooks Hooks, cfg Config) *Consumer {
237		// Memo TTL for bounded consumers: each MaxDeliver attempt holds the message
238		// for at most AckWait before the NakDelay-spaced redelivery. Unlimited
239		// consumers use the fallback below; their memo remains an optimization and
240		// may republish successful routes after a long-running outage.
241		memoTTL := time.Duration(cfg.MaxDeliver) * (cfg.AckWait + cfg.NakDelay)
242		if memoTTL <= 0 {
243			memoTTL = 10 * time.Minute
244		}
245		return &Consumer{js: js, decoder: decoder, resolver: resolver, regions: regions, hooks: hooks, cfg: cfg,
246			memo: newRouteMemo(memoTTL, memoMaxEntries)}
247	}
248	
249	// ensureInactiveThreshold reconciles Config.InactiveThreshold onto an
250	// already-existing durable before the subscribe. The legacy PullSubscribe
251	// BINDS to an existing consumer and silently ignores a requested
252	// InactiveThreshold (nats.go checkConfig does not compare it), so without
253	// this the option would only apply to freshly created durables — a silent
254	// no-op on the live fleet. Read-modify-write keeps every other field exactly
255	// as the server has it; concurrent replicas write the same value, so the race
256	// is benign. Best-effort: on any error the subscribe proceeds — a missing
257	// threshold just degrades to the pre-threshold behavior, and the next Run
258	// iteration retries.
259	func (c *Consumer) ensureInactiveThreshold() {
260		if c.cfg.InactiveThreshold <= 0 || c.cfg.Stream == "" {
261			return
262		}
263		info, err := c.js.ConsumerInfo(c.cfg.Stream, c.cfg.Durable)
264		if err != nil {
265			// Not-found is the fresh-durable case: the subscribe below creates it
266			// WITH the threshold (the create path sends the full config).
267			if !errors.Is(err, nats.ErrConsumerNotFound) && !errors.Is(err, nats.ErrStreamNotFound) {
268				slog.Warn("InactiveThreshold reconcile: consumer lookup failed; proceeding without update",
269					slog.String("stream", c.cfg.Stream), slog.String("durable", c.cfg.Durable), slog.Any("error", err))
270			}
271			return
272		}
273		if info.Config.InactiveThreshold == c.cfg.InactiveThreshold {
274			return
275		}
276		updated := info.Config
277		updated.InactiveThreshold = c.cfg.InactiveThreshold
278		if _, err := c.js.UpdateConsumer(c.cfg.Stream, &updated); err != nil {
279			slog.Warn("InactiveThreshold reconcile: consumer update failed; proceeding without update",
280				slog.String("stream", c.cfg.Stream), slog.String("durable", c.cfg.Durable), slog.Any("error", err))
281			return
282		}
283		slog.Info("InactiveThreshold reconciled onto existing durable",
284			slog.String("stream", c.cfg.Stream), slog.String("durable", c.cfg.Durable),
285			slog.Duration("inactive_threshold", c.cfg.InactiveThreshold))
286	}
287	
288	// Ready reports whether the consumer currently holds a live pull subscription.
289	// /readyz consults this so a pod that can dial NATS but cannot PullSubscribe
290	// (auth/perm/durable-config problem) is reported NotReady instead of looping on
291	// backoff while pretending healthy.
292	func (c *Consumer) Ready() bool { return c.subscribed.Load() }
293	
294	func (c *Consumer) Run(ctx context.Context) {
295		backoff := backoffInit
296		for {
297			c.subscribed.Store(false)
298			c.ensureInactiveThreshold()
299			subOpts := []nats.SubOpt{
300				nats.ManualAck(),
301				nats.AckWait(c.cfg.AckWait),
302				nats.MaxDeliver(c.cfg.MaxDeliver),
303			}
304			if c.cfg.InactiveThreshold > 0 {
305				subOpts = append(subOpts, nats.InactiveThreshold(c.cfg.InactiveThreshold))
306			}
307			sub, err := c.js.PullSubscribe(c.cfg.Subject, c.cfg.Durable, subOpts...)
308			if err != nil {
309				c.health.SubscribeErr(ctx, "Subscribe failed", err,
310					slog.String("subject", c.cfg.Subject), slog.String("durable", c.cfg.Durable))
311				select {
312				case <-ctx.Done():
313					return
314				case <-time.After(backoff):
315					backoff = min(backoff*2, backoffMax)
316					continue
317				}
318			}
319			backoff = backoffInit
320			c.subscribed.Store(true)
321			slog.Info("Subscribed", slog.String("subject", c.cfg.Subject), slog.String("durable", c.cfg.Durable))
322	
323			c.consumeLoop(ctx, sub)
324			c.subscribed.Store(false)
325	
326			if ctx.Err() != nil {
327				return
328			}
329		}
330	}
331	
332	// messageFetcher is the subset of *nats.Subscription the worker pool needs,
333	// narrowed so the pool can be unit-tested with a fake returning canned batches
334	// without a live JetStream.
335	type messageFetcher interface {
336		Fetch(batch int, opts ...nats.PullOpt) ([]*nats.Msg, error)
337	}
338	
339	func (c *Consumer) consumeLoop(ctx context.Context, sub *nats.Subscription) {
340		if c.cfg.Concurrency >= 1 {
341			c.consumeLoopPool(ctx, sub)
342			return
343		}
344		// Strictly-serial path (Concurrency unset): one Fetch(1) at a time. Identical
345		// to the pre-engine core-fanout / meta-fanout behavior.
346		for {
347			if ctx.Err() != nil {
348				return
349			}
350			msgs, err := sub.Fetch(1, nats.MaxWait(fetchMaxWait))
351			if err != nil {
352				if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) {
353					// An idle poll is progress: connected, stream merely quiet.
354					c.health.Recovered()
355					continue
356				}
357				if nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) {
358					return
359				}
360				c.health.Err(ctx, "Fetch error", err)
361				return
362			}
363			c.health.Recovered()
364			for _, msg := range msgs {
365				c.handleMessage(ctx, msg)
366			}
367		}
368	}
369	
370	// consumeLoopPool pulls FetchBatch deliveries at a time and hands each to a
371	// fixed pool of Concurrency workers, so independent deliveries dispatch in
372	// parallel within one pod. Backpressure is structural: the work channel is
373	// UNBUFFERED, so the fetch loop blocks on the send until a worker is free — the
374	// most un-acked fetched messages in flight is at most FetchBatch + Concurrency,
375	// a function of config, never of backlog. On shutdown the fetch loop stops
376	// fetching but every already-fetched message is still handed to the pool, which
377	// drains the channel to its close (not on ctx.Done), so an in-flight dispatch
378	// always runs to its Ack/Nak/Term. Ported verbatim from cmd/fanout.
379	func (c *Consumer) consumeLoopPool(ctx context.Context, sub messageFetcher) {
380		batch := c.cfg.FetchBatch
381		if batch < 1 {
382			batch = 1
383		}
384		work := make(chan *nats.Msg)
385		var wg sync.WaitGroup
386		wg.Add(c.cfg.Concurrency)
387		for range c.cfg.Concurrency {
388			go func() {
389				defer wg.Done()
390				for msg := range work {
391					if c.hooks.IncActive != nil {
392						c.hooks.IncActive(ctx)
393					}
394					c.handleMessage(ctx, msg)
395					if c.hooks.DecActive != nil {
396						c.hooks.DecActive(ctx)
397					}
398				}
399			}()
400		}
401		defer wg.Wait()
402		defer close(work)
403	
404		for {
405			if ctx.Err() != nil {
406				return
407			}
408			msgs, err := sub.Fetch(batch, nats.MaxWait(fetchMaxWait))
409			if err != nil {
410				if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) {
411					// An idle poll is progress: connected, stream merely quiet.
412					c.health.Recovered()
413					continue
414				}
415				if nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) {
416					return
417				}
418				c.health.Err(ctx, "Fetch error", err)
419				return
420			}
421			c.health.Recovered()
422			if c.hooks.RecordFetchBatch != nil {
423				c.hooks.RecordFetchBatch(ctx, len(msgs))
424			}
425			for _, msg := range msgs {
426				work <- msg
427			}
428		}
429	}
430	
431	func (c *Consumer) handleMessage(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
432		spanName := c.cfg.SpanName
433		if spanName == "" {
434			spanName = c.cfg.Tracer + ".dispatch"
435		}
436		ctx = natsmsg.Extract(ctx, msg)
437		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(c.cfg.Tracer).Start(ctx, spanName,
438			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindConsumer),
439			trace.WithAttributes(
440				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
441				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "receive"),
442				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", msg.Subject),
443			),
444		)
445		defer span.End()
446	
447		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
448			span.SetAttributes(
449				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(meta.Sequence.Stream)),
450				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.delivery_count", int64(meta.NumDelivered)),
451			)
452		}
453	
454		c.Dispatch(ctx, span, msg.Subject, msg.Data, msg)
455	}
456	
457	// Dispatch is the per-message handler: decode → resolve → publish → Ack/Nak/Term,
458	// with optional DLQ capture. It is exported and takes a subject + AckableMsg so
459	// tests can drive it directly with a fake, no live JetStream. subject is the
460	// original delivery subject, carried through for the DLQ record. A panic anywhere
461	// below is recovered and Nak'd — never allowed to crash the consume goroutine
462	// (which would redeliver the unacked message and crash-loop every replica).
463	func (c *Consumer) Dispatch(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, subject string, data []byte, msg AckableMsg) {
464		// outcome tags the dispatch-duration sample with the disposition the message
465		// actually got. Defaults to nak so a panic (handled by the recover defer,
466		// which leaves it nak) or a stray early return is attributed conservatively.
467		// The duration recorder is the OUTERMOST defer (declared first) so it runs
468		// after the recover defer and observes the final outcome.
469		start := time.Now()
470		outcome := OutcomeNak
471		defer func() {
472			if c.hooks.RecordDuration != nil {
473				c.hooks.RecordDuration(ctx, outcome, time.Since(start).Seconds())
474			}
475		}()
476		// deliveryID/event are captured for the recover path: a panic mid-fan-out
477		// on the FINAL delivery must still drop the route memo entry (no redelivery
478		// of this message can consult it again), and its dead-letter/metric should
479		// carry the decoded event name. Empty until decode succeeds — nothing is
480		// memoized under "".
481		var deliveryID, event string
482		defer func() {
483			if r := recover(); r != nil {
484				outcome = c.handlePanic(ctx, span, subject, data, msg, r, deliveryID, event)
485			}
486		}()
487	
488		env, err := c.decoder.Decode(data)
489		if err != nil {
490			span.RecordError(err)
491			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "decode envelope")
492			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
493			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Bad envelope, terminating", slog.Any("error", err))
494			c.deadLetter(ctx, span, ReasonBadEnvelope, subject, Envelope{}, data, numDelivered(msg), err)
495			c.recordDispatch(ctx, eventUnknown, OutcomeTerm, ReasonBadEnvelope)
496			outcome = OutcomeTerm
497			_ = msg.Term()
498			return
499		}
500		deliveryID, event = env.DeliveryID, env.Event
501		if c.cfg.SpanAttrs != nil {
502			c.cfg.SpanAttrs(span, env)
503		}
504	
505		outcome = c.dispatchRoutes(ctx, span, subject, env, data, msg)
506	}
507	
508	// dispatchRoutes is the Resolver-path handler: resolve the envelope into routes,
509	// publish each into its region, and apply the disposition. Routes are
510	// independent — one region failing must not starve the others — so it publishes
511	// ALL routes, then Naks if any failed. Regions that already PubAck'd are
512	// memoized in-process and skipped when the redelivery lands back here; a
513	// redelivery on another replica misses the memo and re-publishes them, which
514	// is safe (idempotent syncs / server-side Nats-Msg-Id dedup where the stream's
515	// window allows — mirror_git_v1's 1s window notably does NOT cover the ~30s
516	// redelivery, which is why the memo exists; see routememo.go). Returns the
517	// outcome for the duration metric. An empty route set is a benign no-op (Ack —
518	// nothing to fan out).
519	func (c *Consumer) dispatchRoutes(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, subject string, env Envelope, data []byte, msg AckableMsg) string {
520		routes, ackReason, err := c.resolver.Resolve(ctx, env.Event, env.DeliveryID, env.ObservedAt, env.Body)
521		if err != nil {
522			var ie *InputError
523			if errors.As(err, &ie) {
524				reason := ReasonInputError
525				if ie.Reason != "" {
526					reason = ie.Reason // consumer-supplied sub-kind, e.g. repo_gone
527				}
528				span.RecordError(err)
529				span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, ie.Error())
530				span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
531				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Resolve input error, terminating",
532					slog.String("delivery_id", env.DeliveryID), slog.String("event", env.Event), slog.Any("error", err))
533				c.deadLetter(ctx, span, reason, subject, env, data, numDelivered(msg), err)
534				c.memo.forget(env.DeliveryID)
535				c.recordDispatch(ctx, env.Event, OutcomeTerm, reason)
536				_ = msg.Term()
537				return OutcomeTerm
538			}
539			return c.nakOrExhaust(ctx, span, subject, env, data, msg, err)
540		}
541	
542		// failedClusterIDs collects the cluster_id (route.Region()) of each route
543		// whose publish failed; routeErrs collects the errors themselves.
544		var failedClusterIDs []string
545		var routeErrs []error
546		skipped := 0
547		for _, route := range routes {
548			if c.memo.succeeded(env.DeliveryID, route.Region()) {
549				// This route already PubAck'd this delivery on a prior attempt
550				// that Nak'd on another route's failure — re-publishing would
551				// re-run the work downstream (mirror_git_v1's 1s dedup window is
552				// long expired by the redelivery).
553				skipped++
554				continue
555			}
556			rerr := c.publishRoute(ctx, route)
557			if rerr != nil {
558				failedClusterIDs = append(failedClusterIDs, route.Region())
559				routeErrs = append(routeErrs, rerr)
560				// cluster_id is the field the pre-engine consumers logged; the source
561				// repo is on the span (entire.source_repo), stamped by the resolver.
562				slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Publish failed for placement; continuing with remaining placements",
563					slog.String("cluster_id", route.Region()), slog.Any("error", rerr))
564				continue
565			}
566			c.memo.record(env.DeliveryID, route.Region())
567		}
568	
569		// Preserve the fan-out telemetry contract the consumers already emit
570		// (entire.dispatch.placements* / failed_cluster_ids) — dashboards key on
571		// these, so the engine keeps the established names even though its internal
572		// term is "route". Could be Config-driven if a non-fan-out consumer ever
573		// needs different labels.
574		span.SetAttributes(
575			attribute.Int("entire.dispatch.placements", len(routes)),
576			attribute.Int("entire.dispatch.placements_failed", len(failedClusterIDs)),
577			attribute.Int("entire.dispatch.placements_skipped", skipped),
578		)
579		if len(failedClusterIDs) > 0 {
580			span.SetAttributes(attribute.StringSlice("entire.dispatch.failed_cluster_ids", failedClusterIDs))
581			// Join ALL route failures (not just the first) so a consumer's ClassifyNak
582			// finds a sentinel like ErrUnmappedRegion whenever ANY route hit it,
583			// regardless of order — an earlier transient error must not mask a later
584			// misconfig that never self-heals. The summary rides in front for a
585			// readable log/span line.
586			summary := fmt.Errorf("publish failed for %d of %d placements (clusters: %s)",
587				len(failedClusterIDs), len(routes), strings.Join(failedClusterIDs, ","))
588			cause := errors.Join(append([]error{summary}, routeErrs...)...)
589			return c.nakOrExhaust(ctx, span, subject, env, data, msg, cause)
590		}
591	
592		c.memo.forget(env.DeliveryID)
593		c.recordDispatch(ctx, env.Event, OutcomeAck, ackReason)
594		_ = msg.Ack()
595		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Dispatched",
596			slog.String("delivery_id", env.DeliveryID), slog.String("event", env.Event),
597			slog.Int("routes", len(routes)), slog.String("ack_reason", ackReason))
598		return OutcomeAck
599	}
600	
601	// publishRoute resolves the route's region to its publish handle and publishes.
602	// A region with no mapping (multi-region misconfig) is a failed route, like a
603	// publish error — it Naks and rides redelivery until the map is fixed.
604	func (c *Consumer) publishRoute(ctx context.Context, route Route) error {
605		js, err := c.regions.resolve(route.Region())
606		if err != nil {
607			return err
608		}
609		return route.Publish(ctx, js)
610	}
611	
612	// nakOrExhaust applies the transient disposition shared by the resolve-error and
613	// publish-failure cases: Nak for redelivery, unless this is the final delivery
614	// and a DLQ is wired, in which case capture + Term so the only durable copy
615	// survives.
616	func (c *Consumer) nakOrExhaust(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, subject string, env Envelope, data []byte, msg AckableMsg, cause error) string {
617		nakReason := ""
618		if c.cfg.ClassifyNak != nil {
619			nakReason = c.cfg.ClassifyNak(ctx, span, cause)
620		}
621		span.RecordError(cause)
622		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "dispatch")
623		// The final delivery is terminal whichever branch runs below — the Term,
624		// or a Nak that JetStream will never redeliver (MaxDeliver reached). Drop
625		// the route memo entry now, so a later SEPARATE message reusing the
626		// delivery id (e.g. a manual GitHub redelivery after the ingest stream's
627		// dedup window) fans out fresh instead of skipping regions.
628		if isFinalDelivery(msg, c.cfg.MaxDeliver) {
629			c.memo.forget(env.DeliveryID)
630		}
631		// On the final delivery a Nak is dropped silently at MaxDeliver (and for a
632		// work-queue stream the un-acked message orphans until max_age). When a DLQ
633		// is wired OR TermOnExhaustion is set, Term instead so the message is removed
634		// cleanly; the DLQ (if any) captures it first for replay.
635		if isFinalDelivery(msg, c.cfg.MaxDeliver) && (c.cfg.DLQ != nil || c.cfg.TermOnExhaustion) {
636			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Dispatch failed; deliveries exhausted, terminating",
637				slog.String("delivery_id", env.DeliveryID), slog.String("event", env.Event), slog.Any("error", cause))
638			c.deadLetter(ctx, span, ReasonMaxDeliveries, subject, env, data, numDelivered(msg), cause)
639			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
640			c.recordDispatch(ctx, env.Event, OutcomeTerm, ReasonMaxDeliveries)
641			_ = msg.Term()
642			return OutcomeTerm
643		}
644		slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Dispatch failed; will redeliver",
645			slog.String("delivery_id", env.DeliveryID), slog.String("event", env.Event),
646			slog.Int("delivery", numDelivered(msg)), slog.Duration("redeliver_in", c.cfg.NakDelay),
647			slog.Any("error", cause))
648		c.recordDispatch(ctx, env.Event, OutcomeNak, nakReason)
649		_ = msg.NakWithDelay(c.cfg.NakDelay)
650		return OutcomeNak
651	}
652	
653	// deadLetter best-effort captures a dead-lettered delivery to the DLQ sink.
654	// No-op when no DLQ is configured. Fails open on a capture error (logs + a span
655	// event; the caller Terms anyway) — the failure is permanent or the deliveries
656	// are exhausted, so holding the message only re-runs doomed work. env is the
657	// zero value when the envelope didn't decode (raw bytes still preserved).
658	func (c *Consumer) deadLetter(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, reason, subject string, env Envelope, data []byte, deliveries int, cause error) {
659		if c.cfg.DLQ == nil {
660			return
661		}
662		dl := DeadLetter{
663			Reason:     reason,
664			Subject:    subject,
665			Envelope:   data,
666			Deliveries: deliveries,
667			Event:      env.Event,
668			DeliveryID: env.DeliveryID,
669			Err:        cause,
670		}
671		if err := c.cfg.DLQ.Capture(ctx, dl); err != nil {
672			span.AddEvent("dlq.capture_failed")
673			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Failed to capture dead-lettered delivery; terminating anyway (fail open)",
674				slog.String("reason", reason), slog.Any("error", err))
675		}
676	}
677	
678	func (c *Consumer) handlePanic(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, subject string, data []byte, msg AckableMsg, recovered any, deliveryID, event string) string {
679		err := fmt.Errorf("panic recovered in %s handler: %v", c.cfg.Tracer, recovered)
680		span.RecordError(err)
681		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "handler panic")
682		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.handler.panicked", true))
683		if c.hooks.RecordPanic != nil {
684			c.hooks.RecordPanic(ctx)
685		}
686		// Terminal either way below (Term, or a Nak past MaxDeliver that will
687		// never redeliver): drop the route memo entry so a later message reusing
688		// the delivery id fans out fresh. Mid-fan-out panics can leave one.
689		if isFinalDelivery(msg, c.cfg.MaxDeliver) {
690			c.memo.forget(deliveryID)
691		}
692		// A Nak on the final delivery leaves the message un-acked and orphaned until
693		// max_age (COR-762). When a DLQ is wired OR TermOnExhaustion is set, Term
694		// instead — draining the poison-pill — and, symmetric with nakOrExhaust,
695		// capture it first so a deterministic panic on delivery MaxDeliver isn't
696		// silently lost outside the DLQ. deadLetter is a no-op when DLQ is nil (the
697		// TermOnExhaustion-only work-queue case). The panic is counted via
698		// RecordPanic above regardless.
699		if isFinalDelivery(msg, c.cfg.MaxDeliver) && (c.cfg.DLQ != nil || c.cfg.TermOnExhaustion) {
700			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Recovered panic on final delivery; terminating (dead-letter captured when a DLQ is wired)",
701				slog.Any("panic", recovered), slog.String("stack", string(debug.Stack())))
702			metricEvent := event
703			if metricEvent == "" {
704				metricEvent = eventUnknown
705			}
706			c.deadLetter(ctx, span, ReasonMaxDeliveries, subject, Envelope{DeliveryID: deliveryID, Event: event}, data, numDelivered(msg), err)
707			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true))
708			c.recordDispatch(ctx, metricEvent, OutcomeTerm, ReasonMaxDeliveries)
709			_ = msg.Term()
710			return OutcomeTerm
711		}
712		slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Recovered panic in handler; naking delivery",
713			slog.Any("panic", recovered), slog.String("stack", string(debug.Stack())))
714		_ = msg.NakWithDelay(c.cfg.NakDelay)
715		return OutcomeNak
716	}
717	
718	func (c *Consumer) recordDispatch(ctx context.Context, event, outcome, reason string) {
719		if c.hooks.RecordDispatch != nil {
720			c.hooks.RecordDispatch(ctx, event, outcome, reason)
721		}
722	}
723	
724	// numDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count, or 0 if metadata is
725	// unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test message).
726	func numDelivered(msg AckableMsg) int {
727		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
728			return int(meta.NumDelivered)
729		}
730		return 0
731	}
732	
733	// isFinalDelivery reports whether this is the last delivery before JetStream
734	// stops redelivering (NumDelivered has reached MaxDeliver), so a transient
735	// failure here is terminal rather than another Nak-and-retry.
736	func isFinalDelivery(msg AckableMsg, maxDeliver int) bool {
737		if maxDeliver <= 0 {
738			return false
739		}
740		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
741			return meta.NumDelivered >= uint64(maxDeliver)
742		}
743		return false
744	}

# forwarded deliveries to webhooks.github.v1.>. After the
            # cmd/fanout split, webhook-ingest no longer publishes
            # mirror.> directly — that moved to the fanout user below.
            - user: "webhook-ingest"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                allow_responses: true
            # webhook-forwarder — consumes webhooks.> and POSTs each delivery to
            # entire-web. Publishes only to webhooks.github.dlq.> — capturing a
            # delivery it dead-letters (mirror-pipeline pkg/webhookdlq, gated on
            # ENTIRE_WEBHOOK_DLQ_ENABLED) onto the webhooks_github_dlq stream. The
            # pod-crash advisory backstop also SUBSCRIBES to this consumer's
            # webhooks_github_v1 advisories (below) to re-capture deliveries the
            # inline path missed; GetMsg's STREAM.MSG.GET PUBLISH is already covered
            # by $JS.API.> below.
            - user: "webhook-forwarder"
              permissions:
                publish:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.github.dlq.>"
                    - "$JS.API.>"
                    # Explicit ack grant for this user's webhooks_github_v1 pull
                    # consumer. allow_responses below covers only ONE reply within
                    # ~2m of delivery, so an ack issued outside that window is
                    # rejected — "Publish Violation ... $JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    # — and a rejected ack leaves the message unsettled, so it
                    # redelivers and the work repeats; on a poison message it pins
                    # the consumer's ack floor. A NATS pod restart is what reliably
                    # pushes acks past the window: this was observed on
                    # webhook-forwarder, core-fanout and fanout during the 2.14.4
                    # roll of eks-prod-us-east-2 (2026-08-10, COR-1223), and
                    # meta-fanout / trails-fanout carry the same latent gap.
                    # entire-core-global and entire-search already hold this grant
                    # for the same reason — this brings the remaining
                    # webhooks_github_v1 consumers in line.
                    - "$JS.ACK.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                subscribe:
                  allow:
                    - "webhooks.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"
                    # Pod-crash advisory backstop (mirror-pipeline #159, COR-465):
                    # subscribe to webhooks_github_v1's consumer advisories so the
                    # backstop re-captures a delivery the inline DLQ path dropped
                    # uncaptured when a pod died between giving up and the capture
                    # publish. Wildcard over the durable token (mirrors mirror-worker
                    # above) — the workload subscribes only to its own
                    # WEBHOOK_FORWARDER_DURABLE; the wildcard just avoids coupling the
                    # grant to a durable name. The GetMsg refetch publishes to
                    # $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.webhooks_github_v1, already covered by
                    # $JS.API.> above (the stream isn't AllowDirect).
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                    - "$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MSG_TERMINATED.webhooks_github_v1.>"
                allow_responses: true

            # (every cell, COR-1021: the native-mirror trigger consumer) and
            # publishes mirror.> sync jobs. Took over the mirror.> publish role
            # that webhook-ingest used to have before the cmd/fanout split. And
            # publishes webhooks.github.dlq.> — capturing a delivery it
            # dead-letters (mirror-pipeline pkg/webhookdlq, gated on
            # ENTIRE_WEBHOOK_DLQ_ENABLED) onto the webhooks_github_dlq stream.
            # The pod-crash advisory backstop also SUBSCRIBES to this consumer's
            # webhooks_github_v1 advisories (below) to re-capture deliveries the
            # inline path missed; GetMsg's STREAM.MSG.GET PUBLISH is already
            # covered by $JS.API.> below.
            #
            # repo.ops.v1.> teardown jobs are NOT published here: since COR-523

                    # the binary decides which events fan out.
                    - "repo_refs_v1.>"
                    - "_INBOX.>"

                    # backstop re-captures a delivery the inline DLQ path dropped
                    # uncaptured when a pod died between giving up and the capture
                    # publish. Wildcard over the durable token (mirrors mirror-worker

                    # per-region durable name. The GetMsg refetch publishes to
                    # $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.webhooks_github_v1, already covered by

            # subscribes the stream and re-publishes each event into every cell's
            # local stream (authorized in every cell via base) so each region's
            # entire-api consumes locally. Fan-out logic lives in the
            # mirror-pipeline binary.

                    - "github_pr.v1.>"

1	// Package jsconsumer is the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold shared by
2	// Entire's decode-and-dispatch consumers. Each of those used to hand-roll the
3	// same lifecycle: jetstream.New → CreateOrUpdateConsumer (durable, explicit
4	// ack, bounded ack-wait, bounded MaxDeliver, filter subject) → Consume → stop
5	// on context cancel; and the same per-message prologue: open a consumer span
6	// (re-parented across the NATS hop), decode the payload, and Term on a decode
7	// error.
8	//
9	// This package owns exactly that scaffold and nothing else. Each consumer
10	// keeps its OWN event type, business dispatch, metrics, and log lines — Start
11	// takes the consumer's message callback, and Process invokes the consumer's
12	// handle with the decoded event and the live span. The handler owns the
13	// message's terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term); Process never touches a
14	// message that decoded.
15	//
16	// The one exception to "disposition stays with the handler" is [Retry], the
17	// scaffold's optional single retry mechanism: the redelivery ladder and the
18	// dead-letter capture it terminates into (ENT-1535). A handler that
19	// configures one calls [Retry.Settle] instead of picking a disposition
20	// itself. The consumer has exactly one redelivery scheduler and it is the
21	// SERVER's: the durable's BackOff ladder, or its AckWait when no ladder is
22	// set. Retry disposes of nothing on the retry path, so that schedule is the
23	// one that runs — see [Retry] for why a plain Nak would skip it entirely.
24	//
25	// [FloorMonitor] is the separate, advisory half: it polls the durable's ack
26	// floor and reports how long it has been stalled. Hand it to a Retry and it
27	// becomes the floor-age circuit breaker — which does NOT identify the message
28	// pinning the floor, because consumer info does not carry that: it acts on a
29	// conjunction of independently true facts, so it may quarantine a message that
30	// was failing alongside the blocker rather than being it (bounded to one per
31	// stall window, and the copy is replayable — see [Retry]). Use the monitor
32	// alone and it is just the health signal, leaving the quarantine decision to
33	// the adopter.
34	//
35	// Lifted from entire-api's internal/jsconsumer (COR-929), folding in the
36	// module's shutdown classification ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr] gates the
37	// consume-error log so a drain during rollout isn't reported as a fault,
38	// COR-923) and an optional [natsmsg.KeepInProgress] heartbeat for consumers
39	// whose handlers legitimately outrun AckWait.
40	package jsconsumer
41	
42	import (
43		"context"
44		"errors"
45		"fmt"
46		"log/slog"

48		"time"

51		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
52		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
53		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
54		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
55	
56		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts"
57		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
58	)

60	const (
61		// DefaultAckWait is how long JetStream waits for an ack before redelivery
62		// when Config.AckWait is zero — comfortably longer than an RPC round-trip
63		// plus a DB upsert, short enough that a stuck message redelivers promptly.
64		DefaultAckWait = 30 * time.Second
65		// DefaultMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream stops redelivering a
66		// message when Config.MaxDeliver is zero.
67		DefaultMaxDeliver = 8
68	)

70	// Config describes the durable consumer to create and how to trace/log it. The
71	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
72	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its
73	// existing on-server filter form exactly.
74	type Config struct {
75		Stream         string        // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
76		Durable        string        // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
77		FilterSubject  string        // set this OR FilterSubjects
78		FilterSubjects []string      // set this OR FilterSubject
79		AckWait        time.Duration // 0 → DefaultAckWait (see EffectiveAckWait)
80		MaxDeliver     int           // 0 → DefaultMaxDeliver (see EffectiveMaxDeliver)
81		SpanName       string        // per-message consumer span name (e.g. "repolifecycle.consume")
82		Name           string        // short consumer name, used as the log prefix
83	
84		// InactiveThreshold mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.InactiveThreshold:
85		// how long the durable may go without an active subscription before the
86		// server deletes it; zero means never (the JetStream default for
87		// durables) UNLESS the stream sets ConsumerLimits.InactiveThreshold — see
88		// the note below. Consumers on interest-retention streams set this so a
89		// decommissioned durable stops pinning every message it would have
90		// received, instead of holding them until the stream's MaxAge.
91		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
92	
93		// MaxAckPending mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxAckPending: the
94		// server-side cap on deliveries outstanding un-acked across ALL replicas
95		// sharing the durable; zero uses the server default (1000), or the stream's
96		// ConsumerLimits.MaxAckPending when it sets one — see the note below.
97		// Distinct from MaxMessages below, which caps only this process's
98		// client-side buffer.
99		//
100		// # Stream ConsumerLimits fill in both zeros
101		//
102		// A stream may carry ConsumerLimits, and the server applies them to any
103		// consumer that left the matching field zero. So on such a stream neither
104		// zero above means what it says: this scaffold's consumers inherit the
105		// STREAM's MaxAckPending instead of 1000, and — the consequential one — an
106		// InactiveThreshold instead of never, which gives the durable a deletion
107		// timer nobody here asked for. A durable deleted that way is recreated from
108		// the stream's DeliverPolicy (all, by default) and replays the retained
109		// backlog, so the cost of the surprise is a replay, not just a gap.
110		//
111		// Set both explicitly on a stream with ConsumerLimits, and read the
112		// durable's STORED config rather than assuming either field above is what is
113		// running. Requests that leave them unset are also what pedantic-mode
114		// clients reject outright (NACK's controller drives fleet Consumer CRs that
115		// way), so a config this scaffold applies quietly can fail to reconcile in
116		// the cluster. Measured in internal/brokersemantics
117		// (TestStreamConsumerLimitsAreInheritedBySilentConsumers).
118		MaxAckPending int
119	
120		// BackOff mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff: the redelivery
121		// ladder, one delay per redelivery, applied in place of AckWait. The
122		// server owns redelivery — this is the one schedule, and [Retry] defers to
123		// it by leaving a failed delivery untouched rather than running a
124		// competing one client-side. JetStream
125		// repeats the last rung once the array runs out, so a short list under a
126		// larger MaxDeliver is not a short ladder.
127		//
128		// Setting it alongside Retry is the intended combination. Its coherence —
129		// total time to the dead-letter branch, agreement with AckWait, rung count
130		// against MaxDeliver — is checked at Start through [Schedule], the same
131		// function fleet CI runs over a rendered NACK Consumer CR.
132		//
133		// Leaving it nil is a choice, not a default: the broker still redelivers,
134		// on AckWait, so the effective ladder becomes AckWait repeated up to
135		// MaxDeliver. [Schedule] models it that way and holds it to the same
136		// bounds, which is usually how an unset BackOff gets caught — an AckWait
137		// sized for one RPC makes a fast, tight retry loop, and one sized for a
138		// slow handler makes a very long one.
139		//
140		// Start always sends this value to CreateOrUpdateConsumer, so a nil also
141		// CLEARS any ladder already on the durable. A consumer whose ladder is
142		// managed declaratively therefore cannot just omit it here — that erases
143		// the managed ladder on every start. Declarative management needs a
144		// bind-only mode that skips consumer creation, which does not exist yet;
145		// until it does, the app states the ladder here.
146		BackOff []time.Duration
147	
148		// Retry is where this consumer's retries END: dead-letter capture, then
149		// settle, plus — when its RetryConfig names a FloorMonitor — the
150		// experimental floor-age circuit breaker. It does NOT schedule
151		// redelivery; BackOff above does. When set, [Process] dead-letters an
152		// undecodable payload instead of Terming it, and the whole schedule
153		// (ladder, AckWait, MaxDeliver, and this Retry's expectations of them) is
154		// validated together at Start. Its MaxDeliver must equal
155		// EffectiveMaxDeliver().
156		//
157		// Handlers reach it through the closure they build, and call
158		// [Retry.Settle] as their one disposition for a failed delivery. Nil
159		// leaves disposition entirely to the handler, as before.
160		Retry *Retry
161	
162		// FloorMonitor runs the durable's ack-floor health signal: [Start] polls
163		// it and [Runner.Stop] joins that poll. Set it to publish the stall as a
164		// gauge, or to drive a quarantine rule of your own, without adopting the
165		// library's automatic breaker.
166		//
167		// Leave it nil when Retry already carries the monitor — Start uses that
168		// one. Naming two different monitors is a Start error: one durable has one
169		// ack floor, and one poll loop should read it.
170		FloorMonitor *FloorMonitor
171	
172		// Tracer opens the per-message consumer span; nil uses the global OTel
173		// tracer provider.
174		Tracer trace.Tracer
175		// Logger receives the scaffold's own log lines (decode-term warnings,
176		// consume errors); nil uses slog.Default.
177		Logger *slog.Logger
178	
179		// KeepInProgress runs a natsmsg.KeepInProgress heartbeat while handle
180		// executes, for handlers that legitimately outrun AckWait. The extension
181		// is capped, so a wedged handler still redelivers — see
182		// natsmsg.KeepInProgress. The heartbeat stops when handle returns; a tick
183		// racing the handler's own terminal Ack/Nak/Term is a client-side no-op
184		// (nats.go marks the message disposed locally) that halts the heartbeat.
185		//
186		// Setting this forces the prefetch to one message (see MaxMessages): the
187		// heartbeat extends only the delivery the handler holds, so anything
188		// buffered behind a long handler would exhaust its AckWait unextended.
189		KeepInProgress bool
190	
191		// MaxMessages caps how many deliveries the consume loop buffers
192		// client-side (jetstream.PullMaxMessages); 0 uses the nats.go default
193		// (500). AckWait runs from server delivery into that buffer, not from
194		// callback dispatch, and callbacks run serially — so a consumer whose
195		// handler can approach AckWait should keep this small or queued
196		// deliveries expire and redeliver concurrently to other replicas.
197		// KeepInProgress forces it to 1; setting both to conflicting values is a
198		// Start error.
199		MaxMessages int
200	}

202	// EffectiveAckWait is the AckWait actually applied to the JetStream consumer:
203	// Config.AckWait, or DefaultAckWait when zero. Use it — not the raw field —
204	// anywhere the real value matters, e.g. wiring a natsmsg.KeepInProgress
205	// heartbeat by hand (a zero ackWait there is a no-op).
206	func (c Config) EffectiveAckWait() time.Duration {
207		if c.AckWait == 0 {
208			return DefaultAckWait
209		}
210		return c.AckWait
211	}
212	
213	// EffectiveMaxDeliver is the MaxDeliver actually applied to the JetStream
214	// consumer: Config.MaxDeliver, or DefaultMaxDeliver when zero. Use it — not
215	// the raw field — when building a backoff.Policy for this consumer's
216	// messages: the two packages read zero differently (here it means "default
217	// to DefaultMaxDeliver"; on the policy it means unlimited redeliveries, the
218	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig semantics), so passing a zero Config.MaxDeliver

220	// real final delivery and orphan work-queue messages (COR-762).
221	func (c Config) EffectiveMaxDeliver() int {
222		if c.MaxDeliver == 0 {
223			return DefaultMaxDeliver
224		}
225		return c.MaxDeliver
226	}

229	// [Start] (one-shot) and [Run] (supervised, which must fail fast on these
230	// rather than retry them forever).

233			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): KeepInProgress requires MaxMessages <= 1: the heartbeat extends only the in-flight delivery, so %d buffered messages would exhaust AckWait behind a long handler", c.Name, c.MaxMessages)

236			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Stream is required", c.Name)
237		}
238		if c.Durable == "" {
239			// CreateOrUpdateConsumer accepts an empty durable and silently makes
240			// an ephemeral, server-named consumer — losing the stable

440		}

443	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
444	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
445	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
446	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
447	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
448	//
449	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
450	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
451	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
452	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
453		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
454			return nil, err
455		}
456		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
457		if err != nil {
458			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
459		}
460		if err := cfg.checkAgainstStream(ctx, js); err != nil {
461			return nil, err
462		}
463		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
464			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
465			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
466			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
467			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
468			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
469			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
470			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
471			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
472			// Always sent, so an update carries it — and so a nil CLEARS whatever
473			// ladder the durable had, leaving AckWait as the schedule. That is
474			// why a declaratively-managed ladder cannot simply be omitted here:
475			// see Config.BackOff.
476			BackOff: cfg.BackOff,
477		})
478		if err != nil {
479			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
480		}
481		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {

483				return
484			}

486		})}
487		switch {
488		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
489			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
490		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:

492		}

494		if err != nil {
495			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
496		}
497		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
498		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
499		if cfg.Retry != nil {

504			pollDone := make(chan struct{})

507				defer close(pollDone)

509			}()
510		}
511		go func() {
512			defer close(watcherDone)
513			select {
514			case <-ctx.Done():

516			case <-r.closed:
517			}

522	// isRetryableStartError classifies the narrow set of failures that can become
523	// healthy without changing Config or replacing nc. Everything else returns to
524	// the owner so a bad deployment cannot stay alive indefinitely with no

526	// permanent JetStream configuration/account errors whose API happens to use a
527	// 5xx status.
528	func isRetryableStartError(err error) bool {
529		if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
530			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
531			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
532			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrDisconnected) {
533			return true
534		}

536		var jsErr jetstream.JetStreamError
537		if !errors.As(err, &jsErr) || jsErr.APIError() == nil {
538			return false
539		}
540		apiErr := jsErr.APIError()
541		switch apiErr.ErrorCode { //nolint:exhaustive // unrecognized 5xx codes are deliberately retryable; all other unknown codes fail closed
542		case jetstream.JSErrCodeBadRequest,
543			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerCreate,
544			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerNameExists,

559	// Retry envelope for [Run]'s supervision: exponential from runRetryInitial
560	// doubling to runRetryMax, reset once a consume loop survives longer than the
561	// max. Package vars (not consts) so tests can compress the schedule.
562	var (
563		runRetryInitial = time.Second
564		runRetryMax     = 30 * time.Second
565	)
566	
567	// Run supervises the consume loop [Start] builds. Where Start is one-shot —
568	// an error at consumer creation is returned, and a consume loop that closes
569	// underneath the caller (consumer deleted on the server, subscription
570	// invalidated) stays closed — Run retries both with exponential backoff
571	// (runRetryInitial doubling to runRetryMax, reset after a loop that outlives
572	// the max). In particular a stream that is not provisioned yet at boot — the
573	// declarative-provisioning race — is a retry, not a crash.
574	//
575	// Run blocks until ctx is cancelled, then joins the live loop (including an
576	// in-flight handler, see [Runner.Stop]) before returning, so it composes with
577	// the cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering as the body of a supervised
578	// goroutine:
579	//
580	//	g.Go(func(ctx context.Context) {
581	//		if err := jsconsumer.Run(ctx, nc, cfg, onMsg); err != nil {
582	//			log.Error("consumer config rejected", "error", err)
583	//		}
584	//	})
585	//
586	// Local configuration errors and permanent server responses (invalid consumer
587	// configuration, authorization/account setup) can never succeed on retry and
588	// are returned immediately. A missing declarative stream, temporary transport
589	// failure, or unknown server-side 5xx response remains supervised. A nil return
590	// means a clean, ctx-driven exit.
591	func Run(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
592		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
593			return err
594		}
595		delay := runRetryInitial
596		for {
597			// Each attempt gets a child context so the cancel-watcher goroutine
598			// Start arms is released when the attempt dies, instead of one
599			// accumulating per recreate for the life of the process.
600			attemptCtx, cancelAttempt := context.WithCancel(ctx)
601			r, err := Start(attemptCtx, nc, cfg, onMsg)
602			if err != nil {
603				cancelAttempt()
604				if ctx.Err() != nil {
605					return nil //nolint:nilerr // a Start error during shutdown is a clean, ctx-driven exit, not a fault to report
606				}
607				if !isRetryableStartError(err) {
608					return err
609				}
610				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": start consumer failed; retrying",
611					slog.Any("error", err), slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
612			} else {
613				started := time.Now()
614				select {
615				case <-ctx.Done():
616					r.Stop()
617					cancelAttempt()
618					return nil
619				case <-r.closed:
620					// Join before recreating, not just cancel: the attempt's
621					// ack-floor poll may still be in an in-flight consumer-info
622					// request against the OLD consumer, and the next Start attaches
623					// the same monitor to a new one. Without the join that reply
624					// can land after the reattach and overwrite fresh state with
625					// stale. Stop is cheap here — the loop has already closed.
626					r.Stop()
627					cancelAttempt()
628					if ctx.Err() != nil {
629						return nil //nolint:nilerr // the loop closing during shutdown is the expected wind-down, not a fault
630					}
631					// A loop that ran long enough to be called healthy earns a
632					// fresh envelope; a flapping one keeps escalating.
633					if time.Since(started) >= runRetryMax {
634						delay = runRetryInitial
635					}
636					cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume loop closed; recreating",
637						slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
638				}
639			}
640			select {
641			case <-ctx.Done():
642				return nil
643			case <-time.After(delay):
644			}
645			delay = min(delay*2, runRetryMax)
646		}
647	}
648	
649	// Process runs the per-message prologue shared by every consumer: open the
650	// consumer span (re-parented to the producer across the NATS hop), decode the
651	// payload, and on a decode error record it, log "<Name>: decode <Stream>;
652	// term", invoke onUndecodable (so the caller bumps its own drop metric with
653	// its own attributes), and Term the message — a poison payload won't decode on
654	// redelivery. On success it invokes handle with the span-enriched context, the
655	// live span (for RecordError/SetStatus on the business error paths), the
656	// message, and the decoded event; with Config.KeepInProgress set, an AckWait
657	// heartbeat runs for the duration of handle.
658	//
659	// Callers wire Process as the func they pass to Start AND the entry point
660	// their tests drive, so the decode-or-term path is exercised the same way in
661	// production and tests.
662	func Process[E any](
663		ctx context.Context,
664		msg jetstream.Msg,
665		cfg Config,
666		decode func([]byte) (E, error),
667		handle func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev E),
668		onUndecodable func(ctx context.Context),
669	) {
670		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, cfg.tracer(), msg, cfg.SpanName)
671		defer span.End()
672	
673		ev, err := decode(msg.Data())
674		if err != nil {
675			span.RecordError(err)
676			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "decode")
677			disposition := "term"
678			if cfg.Retry != nil {
679				disposition = "dead-letter"
680			}
681			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": decode "+cfg.Stream+"; "+disposition,
682				slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
683			if onUndecodable != nil {
684				onUndecodable(ctx)
685			}
686			if cfg.Retry != nil {
687				// Same terminal effect as the Term below, but the payload
688				// survives: a bare Term settles the message perfectly well, it
689				// just leaves no trace of what was discarded — the last
690				// drop-without-a-record surface in this scaffold, and a Retry is
691				// exactly the capture path that closes it.
692				if _, dlErr := cfg.Retry.DeadLetter(ctx, msg, "undecodable: "+err.Error()); dlErr != nil {
693					cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": dead-letter undecodable failed", slog.Any("error", dlErr))
694				}
695				return
696			}
697			if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
698				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": term failed", slog.Any("error", termErr))
699			}
700			return
701		}
702		if cfg.KeepInProgress {
703			stop := natsmsg.KeepInProgress(msg.InProgress, cfg.EffectiveAckWait())
704			defer stop()
705		}
706		handle(ctx, span, msg, ev)

1	package jsconsumer

3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6		"time"
7	
8		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/backoff"
9	)
10	
11	// UnlimitedMaxDeliver mirrors [backoff.UnlimitedMaxDeliver] and
12	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver: a non-positive cap means the broker
13	// redelivers forever.
14	const UnlimitedMaxDeliver = backoff.UnlimitedMaxDeliver
15	
16	// Schedule is a durable consumer's retry timing as plain values, and
17	// [Schedule.Validate] is the single implementation of the arithmetic that
18	// says whether it hangs together.
19	//
20	// It takes values rather than a live consumer or a [RetryConfig] on purpose.
21	// The same arithmetic has to run in three places — [NewRetry] at construction,
22	// a fleet CI lint over rendered NACK Consumer CRs before merge, and (when
23	// bind-only mode lands) the library at startup against the durable's ACTUAL
24	// server-side config — and three implementations of it would drift. ENT-1535
25	// was a consumer whose real redelivery envelope was 34h22m while its config
26	// advertised 17h45m; duplicated timing arithmetic is precisely how that
27	// happens. Compile this function into the checker instead of restating it.
28	//
29	// Validate is pure: no NATS connection, no I/O, no clock. Zero-valued fields
30	// are "not known / not constrained" and their checks are skipped, so a caller
31	// that knows only the server-side ladder still gets every check that ladder
32	// supports.
33	type Schedule struct {
34		// NakDelay, Factor and MaxDelay describe the CLIENT-side ladder the
35		// library applies with NakWithDelay (see backoff.Policy). Leave NakDelay
36		// zero when the server owns redelivery.
37		NakDelay time.Duration
38		Factor   float64
39		MaxDelay time.Duration
40	
41		// ServerBackOff is the SERVER-side ladder from the consumer's own config
42		// (jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff, or a NACK Consumer CR's backOff).
43		// Leave it empty when the client owns redelivery. Setting both this and
44		// NakDelay is the ENT-1535 defect itself and is reported as a violation.
45		ServerBackOff []time.Duration
46	
47		// MaxDeliver is the consumer's delivery cap, AckWait its redelivery
48		// timeout. Zero means unknown; [UnlimitedMaxDeliver] (or any non-positive
49		// value) means the consumer never stops redelivering, which has no
50		// terminal branch and so no duration to bound.
51		MaxDeliver int
52		AckWait    time.Duration
53	
54		// CaptureReserve is how many deliveries are held back to retry a failed
55		// dead-letter capture, so the ladder's terminal branch is reached at
56		// MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve.
57		CaptureReserve int
58	
59		// MaxTimeToDeadLetter bounds the cumulative scheduled wait to that
60		// terminal branch. Zero leaves it unbounded.
61		MaxTimeToDeadLetter time.Duration
62	
63		// RecoverBy is the delivery by which a transient failure is expected to
64		// clear, and FloorAge the stall threshold a floor-age breaker would act
65		// on. Both are client-side expectations; zero means not applicable.
66		RecoverBy int
67		FloorAge  time.Duration
68	
69		// StreamMaxAge is the stream's retention window. A ladder that outlives it
70		// cannot reach its own terminal branch — the message is discarded first.
71		// Zero means unknown or unlimited.
72		StreamMaxAge time.Duration
73	}
74	
75	// Violation is one way a [Schedule] does not hang together.
76	type Violation struct {
77		// Field names the setting to change, in the caller's own vocabulary where
78		// they differ (a CR's backOff is this type's ServerBackOff).
79		Field string
80		// Problem states what is wrong and what it costs, in one sentence.
81		Problem string
82	}
83	
84	func (v Violation) String() string { return v.Field + ": " + v.Problem }
85	
86	// Ladder reports the client-side ladder as a backoff.Policy.
87	func (s Schedule) Ladder() backoff.Policy {
88		return backoff.Policy{NakDelay: s.NakDelay, Factor: s.Factor, MaxDelay: s.MaxDelay, MaxDeliver: s.MaxDeliver}
89	}
90	
91	// DeadLetterDelivery is the delivery on which the terminal branch is reached:
92	// the delivery cap less whatever is reserved for retrying a failed capture.
93	func (s Schedule) DeadLetterDelivery() int { return s.MaxDeliver - s.CaptureReserve }
94	
95	// RungBefore is the scheduled wait served before delivery number n (n >= 2),
96	// from whichever mechanism actually schedules this consumer's redeliveries, in
97	// precedence order:
98	//
99	//  1. ServerBackOff — the durable's ladder. JetStream repeats the LAST rung
100	//     once the array runs out, so a short list under a larger maxDeliver is
101	//     not a short ladder.
102	//  2. NakDelay — a client-scheduled ladder, for modelling a legacy consumer
103	//     that Naks with its own delays. Nothing in this package produces one.
104	//  3. AckWait — NO ladder at all. This is not "no wait": with an empty
105	//     BackOff the broker still redelivers, on the acknowledgement timeout, so
106	//     the real ladder is AckWait repeated. Treating that case as zero made
107	//     every duration check pass vacuously — an AckWait of 1h with MaxDeliver 6
108	//     scored as an instant schedule while really taking four hours to reach
109	//     the dead-letter branch.
110	//
111	// Every timing check goes through here rather than reading the fields
112	// directly, because each time one didn't, it silently measured a ladder that
113	// was not the one running.
114	func (s Schedule) RungBefore(n int) time.Duration {
115		switch {
116		case n < 2:
117			return 0
118		case len(s.ServerBackOff) > 0:
119			return s.ServerBackOff[min(n-2, len(s.ServerBackOff)-1)]
120		case s.NakDelay > 0:
121			return s.Ladder().DelayFor(n - 1)
122		default:
123			return s.AckWait
124		}
125	}
126	
127	// CumulativeTo is the total scheduled wait a message has served by the time it
128	// is delivered for the nth time.
129	func (s Schedule) CumulativeTo(n int) time.Duration {
130		var total time.Duration
131		for i := 2; i <= n; i++ {
132			total += s.RungBefore(i)
133		}
134		return total
135	}
136	
137	// LongestRung is the largest wait this schedule ever serves before the
138	// terminal branch.
139	func (s Schedule) LongestRung() time.Duration {
140		var longest time.Duration
141		for i := 2; i <= s.DeadLetterDelivery(); i++ {
142			longest = max(longest, s.RungBefore(i))
143		}
144		return longest
145	}
146	
147	// TimeToDeadLetter is the cumulative scheduled wait before the terminal branch
148	// runs — the number a stall SLA is actually about. It counts scheduled waits
149	// only; handler time and a lost delivery's AckWait sit on top.
150	func (s Schedule) TimeToDeadLetter() time.Duration {
151		return s.CumulativeTo(s.DeadLetterDelivery())
152	}
153	
154	// Validate reports every way the schedule does not hang together, most
155	// structural first. An empty result means it is coherent.
156	//
157	//nolint:gocognit // one flat list of independent checks; splitting it would scatter the arithmetic this type exists to centralize
158	func (s Schedule) Validate() []Violation {
159		var vs []Violation
160		add := func(field, format string, args ...any) {
161			vs = append(vs, Violation{Field: field, Problem: fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)})
162		}
163	
164		// The ENT-1535 defect itself: two schedulers, so neither is the real one.
165		if s.NakDelay > 0 && len(s.ServerBackOff) > 0 {
166			add("ServerBackOff", "set with a client-side NakDelay (%s): the server stretches each NAK delay by the BackOff increments, so redeliveries follow neither ladder and the configured one becomes dead config", s.NakDelay)
167		}
168		if s.NakDelay < 0 {
169			add("NakDelay", "must not be negative, got %s", s.NakDelay)
170		}
171		if s.Factor > 1 && s.MaxDelay <= 0 {
172			add("MaxDelay", "required with a growing Factor (%.1f): an uncapped rung cannot be checked against any bound", s.Factor)
173		}
174		for i, d := range s.ServerBackOff {
175			if d <= 0 {
176				add("ServerBackOff", "rung %d must be positive, got %s", i, d)
177			}
178		}
179		if s.MaxTimeToDeadLetter < 0 {
180			add("MaxTimeToDeadLetter", "must not be negative, got %s", s.MaxTimeToDeadLetter)
181		}
182		// Non-positive means UNLIMITED redeliveries, matching
183		// jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver and backoff.UnlimitedMaxDeliver.
184		// Only a value below that sentinel is nonsense. An unlimited consumer has
185		// no terminal branch, so every duration check below is skipped rather
186		// than being computed against a delivery number that does not exist.
187		if s.MaxDeliver < UnlimitedMaxDeliver {
188			add("MaxDeliver", "must be -1 (unlimited) or positive, got %d", s.MaxDeliver)
189		}
190		if s.CaptureReserve < 0 {
191			add("CaptureReserve", "must not be negative, got %d", s.CaptureReserve)
192		}
193		if s.MaxDeliver > 0 && s.CaptureReserve >= s.MaxDeliver {
194			add("CaptureReserve", "%d leaves no deliveries for the handler out of MaxDeliver %d", s.CaptureReserve, s.MaxDeliver)
195		}
196	
197		// A server ladder must have somewhere to apply every rung. The bound
198		// mirrors the server's own (it rejects len(BackOff) > MaxDeliver, despite
199		// error text implying strict >), so the equal case stays legal here too —
200		// suspicious rather than wrong, since MaxDeliver deliveries leave only
201		// MaxDeliver-1 redeliveries and that last rung is never served.
202		if n := len(s.ServerBackOff); n > 0 && s.MaxDeliver > 0 && n > s.MaxDeliver {
203			add("ServerBackOff", "has %d rungs but MaxDeliver %d schedules at most %d of them: %d deliveries leave %d redeliveries", n, s.MaxDeliver, s.MaxDeliver-1, s.MaxDeliver, s.MaxDeliver-1)
204		}
205		// The server does not run a consumer whose AckWait disagrees with its first
206		// rung: on the ordinary create/update path it silently REWRITES the stored
207		// AckWait to BackOff[0] (measured in internal/brokersemantics,
208		// REDACTED). So the redelivery timing is
209		// knowable — it is the ladder — and what the declared AckWait becomes is a
210		// value nothing on the server ever holds. That is worth a violation for two
211		// reasons: the config lies to whoever reads it, and a pedantic-mode client
212		// rejects the same request outright rather than normalizing it, so a
213		// mismatch this scaffold would apply quietly fails to reconcile under
214		// NACK's controller.
215		if len(s.ServerBackOff) > 0 && s.AckWait > 0 && s.AckWait != s.ServerBackOff[0] {
216			add("AckWait", "%s disagrees with ServerBackOff[0] (%s): the server stores the first rung in place of it, so the declared AckWait never runs — and a pedantic-mode create rejects the mismatch instead of rewriting it", s.AckWait, s.ServerBackOff[0])
217		}
218	
219		if s.MaxDeliver <= 0 || s.DeadLetterDelivery() < 1 {
220			return vs // nothing below can be computed
221		}
222		ttl := s.TimeToDeadLetter()
223	
224		if s.MaxTimeToDeadLetter > 0 && ttl > s.MaxTimeToDeadLetter {
225			add("MaxTimeToDeadLetter", "the ladder takes %s to reach the dead-letter branch (delivery %d), past the %s bound: shorten the rungs, lower MaxDeliver, or raise the bound", ttl, s.DeadLetterDelivery(), s.MaxTimeToDeadLetter)
226		}
227		// A ladder that outlives retention never reaches its own terminal branch.
228		if s.StreamMaxAge > 0 && ttl >= s.StreamMaxAge {
229			add("StreamMaxAge", "the ladder takes %s to reach the dead-letter branch but the stream discards after %s: the message is gone before it can be captured", ttl, s.StreamMaxAge)
230		}
231	
232		if s.RecoverBy < 0 {
233			add("RecoverBy", "must not be negative, got %d", s.RecoverBy)
234		}
235		if s.RecoverBy > s.DeadLetterDelivery() {
236			add("RecoverBy", "%d exceeds the ladder's %d deliveries: recovery is expected after the ladder has already given up", s.RecoverBy, s.DeadLetterDelivery())
237		}
238		if s.FloorAge > 0 {
239			// The ladder and the breaker threshold are one schedule: if the wait
240			// to the expected recovery reaches the threshold, the breaker can
241			// quarantine a transient that was still going to succeed.
242			if s.RecoverBy > 0 && s.RecoverBy <= s.DeadLetterDelivery() {
243				if cum := s.CumulativeTo(s.RecoverBy); cum >= s.FloorAge {
244					add("RecoverBy", "the ladder reaches delivery %d after %s, at or past FloorAge (%s): a transient still inside its recovery window could be dead-lettered — shorten the ladder, lower RecoverBy, or raise FloorAge", s.RecoverBy, cum, s.FloorAge)
245				}
246			}
247			// A threshold the ladder never reaches is a breaker that can never
248			// fire — configured, named in every doc and dashboard, and inert. The
249			// ENT-1535 disease in miniature, so it is a violation rather than a
250			// quiet no-op. The breaker's last chance is the dead-letter delivery
251			// itself, since Settle weighs quarantine before exhaustion.
252			//
253			// Note the weaker case this does NOT reject: a threshold above
254			// CumulativeTo(DeadLetterDelivery-1) leaves the breaker able to fire
255			// only on the very delivery exhaustion would have handled anyway, so
256			// it accelerates nothing. That is a judgement about whether the
257			// breaker earns its keep on a given ladder, not a broken config, and
258			// on a tight bounded ladder it is the normal outcome.
259			if ttl := s.TimeToDeadLetter(); ttl > 0 && s.FloorAge > ttl {
260				add("FloorAge", "%s is longer than the %s this ladder takes to dead-letter a message: the breaker could never fire — shorten FloorAge, lengthen the ladder, or drop the monitor",
261					s.FloorAge, ttl)
262			}
263			// A breaker only ever fires on a delivery, so a rung longer than the
264			// threshold leaves the floor pinned for that rung after it arms.
265			if rung := s.LongestRung(); rung > s.FloorAge {
266				add("FloorAge", "the largest ladder rung (%s) exceeds FloorAge (%s): the breaker acts on a delivery, so the floor would stay pinned for up to FloorAge+%s", rung, s.FloorAge, rung)
267			}
268		}
269		return vs
270	}
271	
272	// Err folds Validate's result into a single error, or nil when the schedule is
273	// coherent — the form [NewRetry] and a bind-time check want, where fleet CI
274	// wants the individual violations.
275	func (s Schedule) Err() error {
276		vs := s.Validate()
277		if len(vs) == 0 {
278			return nil
279		}
280		parts := make([]string, 0, len(vs))
281		for _, v := range vs {
282			parts = append(parts, v.String())
283		}
284		return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: incoherent retry schedule: %s", strings.Join(parts, "; "))
285	}
